@about: Help for every command (app/CommandHelp.hpp): one record per command id. Translations by id in commands.<language>.json.

commands.title: New document
commands.summary: Starts a new, empty OPAD design.
commands.details: The current document is closed first; if it has unsaved changes you are asked whether to save them. The new design has no file until you save it.

commands.title: Open
commands.summary: Opens an OPAD document, a CAD model, a mesh or a 2D drawing.
commands.details: OPAD documents open for editing. STEP, IGES, STL, 3MF, OBJ, DXF, DWG, SVG and the other formats open read-only in viewer mode, which is fast; Save turns them into editable OPAD documents.

commands.title: Clone repository
commands.summary: Copies a git repository to this computer and opens its OPAD documents.
commands.details: Type the address, the folder it goes into and its name, then Clone. The copy is set up for OPAD's merge and difference tools, and its .opad documents are offered to open.
commands.requires: git must be installed; Locate git… points OPAD to it.

commands.title: Compare versions
commands.summary: Shows two versions of the document in one view: what was added, removed, changed or moved.
commands.details: Pick A and B in the Compare panel: this session, the saved file, git commits, recovery snapshots or another file. The view draws B tinted by change with ghosts of A, the panel lists the changes and Next change ({key:vcs.nextChange}) steps through them; Done or {fixed:esc} ends it.
commands.requires: Open an OPAD document; not while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Show unsaved changes
commands.summary: Compares the saved file with this session: what changed since the last save.
commands.details: It opens Compare with the saved file as A and this session as B. The unsaved-changes question offers it too, as Review changes.
commands.requires: Only for a saved OPAD document with unsaved changes.

commands.title: Version control
commands.summary: Opens the Version control panel: the branch and its remote, the document's state, its history and the branches.
commands.details: Commit, push, pull and switch branches from there; the git chip beside the path opens it too. A document that is not in a repository yet is offered one.
commands.requires: Save the document as an OPAD file first; a viewed file cannot be versioned.

commands.title: Commit
commands.summary: Records the document (saved first) and the files you tick in git, with a message.
commands.details: The message is suggested from what changed since the last commit, and the author is asked for once. You can amend the last commit while it is not pushed, and push right after.
commands.requires: Save the document as an OPAD file first; a viewed file cannot be versioned.

commands.title: Push
commands.summary: Sends your commits to the remote repository.
commands.details: The first push sets up the remote branch, adding a remote when there is none, and warns about big files. Commit first: a branch with no commits has nothing to push.
commands.requires: Save the document as an OPAD file first; a viewed file cannot be versioned.

commands.title: Pull
commands.summary: Fetches the remote's commits and shows what they change in the document before merging them.
commands.details: Conflicts and changes made on both sides are listed, with Preview in Compare and Merge. The branch must follow a remote branch; Push sets that up.
commands.requires: Save the document as an OPAD file first; a viewed file cannot be versioned.

commands.title: Fetch
commands.summary: Downloads the remote's new commits without changing your files.
commands.details: The git chip then shows how far ahead of or behind the remote your branch is. Fetch in the background does it every 10 minutes, quietly.
commands.requires: Save the document as an OPAD file first; a viewed file cannot be versioned.

commands.title: New branch
commands.summary: Starts a branch at the current commit to try a variant of the design.
commands.details: Name it in the dialog; History can also start a branch from an older commit. Commit first: a branch starts at a commit.
commands.requires: Save the document as an OPAD file first; a viewed file cannot be versioned.

commands.title: History
commands.summary: Lists the commits of the document in the Version control panel.
commands.details: Compare a commit with this session or with the commit before, open it read-only, restore it as new changes, or start a branch from it. Show in version history on a timeline marker narrows the list to the commits that touched that step.
commands.requires: Save the document as an OPAD file first; a viewed file cannot be versioned.

commands.title: Branches
commands.summary: Lists the branches: switch to one, create, delete or merge one into the current branch.
commands.details: Unsaved and uncommitted changes are asked about before a switch, and a merge shows what it brings in first. Abort merge is there while a merge stopped on conflicts.
commands.requires: Save the document as an OPAD file first; a viewed file cannot be versioned.

commands.title: Pack the repository
commands.summary: Packs the repository's loose objects so it takes less space.
commands.details: It runs git's maintenance on a worker and says what it saved. After a commit it is offered when many loose objects have piled up.
commands.requires: Save the document as an OPAD file first; a viewed file cannot be versioned.

commands.title: Resolve conflicts
commands.summary: Settles a merge that stopped on the document, change by change.
commands.details: What both sides changed is listed: choose mine or theirs for each, or keep a whole side. The file is then written and added, Regenerate is offered, and you commit the merge.
commands.requires: Save the document as an OPAD file first; a viewed file cannot be versioned.

commands.title: Fetch in the background
commands.summary: Fetches from the remote every 10 minutes, quietly.
commands.details: It never asks for a sign-in; turn it off on a metered or slow connection. Fetch does it once by hand.

commands.title: Next change
commands.summary: Goes to the next change in Compare.
commands.details: Its row in the panel is selected and its bodies are fitted in the view. Previous change ({key:vcs.previousChange}) goes back.
commands.requires: Only while Compare is open.

commands.title: Previous change
commands.summary: Goes to the previous change in Compare.
commands.details: Its row in the panel is selected and its bodies are fitted in the view. Next change ({key:vcs.nextChange}) goes forward.
commands.requires: Only while Compare is open.

commands.title: Import
commands.summary: Adds a CAD model, mesh or drawing file to this design.
commands.details: The file's parts join the open document as new bodies, under the selected component if you choose to. A 2D drawing asks where it goes: onto a selected planar face, or on a plane you pick and place. A KiCad board first asks what to build.
commands.requires: A file in viewer mode asks you to save it as an OPAD document first.

commands.title: Save as OPAD document
commands.summary: Saves the file open in viewer mode as an editable OPAD document.
commands.details: The shapes already on screen are kept, so nothing is read again. The file you opened is left as it is; from then on you edit the new .opad document.
commands.requires: Only for a file open in viewer mode (STEP, STL, DXF and the other formats).

commands.title: Link as asset
commands.summary: Brings a CAD model, mesh, picture or drawing into the design as a link: the document keeps a reference and reads the file whenever it opens.
commands.details: Choose the file; its parts come in read-only and the document stays small. OPAD watches the file, badges its state in the browser and offers its changes for syncing. A drawing is placed first, on the selected face or on a plane you pick, and a KiCad board first asks how to read it.

commands.title: Sync linked file
commands.summary: Reads the selected linked files again and updates their parts in the design.
commands.details: Parts that changed in the file are updated, new ones are added and removed ones taken out, and the features built on them are recomputed. Each file is one step to undo, and a toast says how many parts changed. A click on the Sync badge of a changed file in the browser does the same.
commands.requires: Select a part of a linked file first; not for a file in viewer mode.

commands.title: Sync all linked files
commands.summary: Syncs every linked file that changed since its last sync.
commands.details: The files are read again one after the other, each as its own step to undo, and a toast says how many were synced. When a watched file changes, a toast offers the same.
commands.requires: Only when a linked file changed since its last sync.

commands.title: Sync changed files automatically
commands.summary: Syncs linked files as soon as OPAD sees that they changed, without asking.
commands.details: Each sync is still one step, and its toast offers Undo. Off, a changed file shows its Sync badge and a toast offers to sync it. A document open read-only still asks, and the choice is kept for the next session.

commands.title: Replace linked file
commands.summary: Points the selected linked file's link at another file and reads its parts from there.
commands.details: Choose the new file: the import is synced from it, its parts updated and the features built on them recomputed. It is one step to undo, and later changes of the new file are watched.
commands.requires: Select a part of one linked file first; not for a file in viewer mode.

commands.title: Show linked file in folder
commands.summary: Opens the folder of the selected linked file in the system's file manager.
commands.details: On Windows the file is selected there. If the file is not found, a toast names the path that was looked for.
commands.requires: Select a part of one linked file first; not for a file in viewer mode.

commands.title: Copy linked file path
commands.summary: Copies the full path of the selected linked file to the clipboard.
commands.details: A toast shows the path that was copied. Paste it into a file dialog, a message or a terminal.
commands.requires: Select a part of one linked file first; not for a file in viewer mode.

commands.title: Embed as editable
commands.summary: Stores the selected linked file's parts in the document, so they can be edited.
commands.details: The link ends: later changes to the file no longer reach the design, and the parts lose their read-only mark and their badge. It is one step to undo.
commands.requires: Select a part of one linked file first; not for a file in viewer mode.

commands.title: Pack into project
commands.summary: Copies the selected linked file into the assets folder beside the document and links that copy.
commands.details: The project then carries the file with it, for a colleague or a git repository. In a git work tree the copy is offered to be tracked with Git LFS. The new link is one step to undo; the copied file stays.
commands.requires: Select a part of one linked file, in a document saved as an OPAD file.

commands.title: Linked files
commands.summary: Sets how STEP, IGES, KiCad boards and big files come in, and which folders are trusted for linked files.
commands.details: Importing those files can ask each time, link them as assets or import an editable copy. Linked files outside a document's project folder are read only once you say so, unless their folder is trusted. The trusted folders are listed here, where Remove takes one off; the question's Always trust this folder adds one. OK keeps the choices.

commands.title: KiCad boards
commands.summary: Sets how KiCad boards are read: the reader, what they include, their origin and where their 3D models are found.
commands.details: Read them with OPAD's board reader, or with KiCad's own STEP export when KiCad is installed, which can add copper, pads and silkscreen. Choose the footprints' 3D models, parts marked do not populate and drilled vias, the boxes shown for missing models, the model folders and whether models of KiCad's library are downloaded. Save keeps it for the next boards and checks the linked ones again.

commands.title: Insert KiCad PCB
commands.summary: Brings a KiCad board (.kicad_pcb) into the design, linked to its file.
commands.details: The Import KiCad board dialog sets how it is read, what it includes and its origin. The board comes in with a component per footprint and its 3D model, plus its outline and mounting holes; the file is watched and its changes are offered for syncing. Models of KiCad's library that are not installed can be downloaded.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Preview KiCad sync
commands.summary: Lists what changed in the selected board's file since its last sync, before you sync it.
commands.details: The Sync preview panel lists the parts moved, flipped, changed, added and removed, the board's own changes and the sketches and features they affect. The parts that change are tinted in the view, and a row selects its part. Sync applies exactly that as one step; Cancel closes it with nothing changed.
commands.requires: Select a part of a linked KiCad board first.

commands.title: Project KiCad board
commands.summary: Brings a board's outline, mounting holes and chosen parts' outlines into the open sketch.
commands.details: Tick what to project: the board outline, the mounting holes (also ones added later) and parts, found with the filter by reference or footprint. Linked, they follow the board when it is synced, so an enclosure drawn on them keeps up with the board.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open, in a document with a KiCad board.

commands.title: Check clearance to board
commands.summary: Checks the gap between a KiCad board's parts and the enclosure around it.
commands.details: The enclosure is the selection outside the board, else every other visible solid. The Board clearance panel lists overlaps and pairs closer than the Clearance you set (1 mm at first); a click on a row selects the pair and shows its gap. The check runs on a worker, and Check runs it again.
commands.requires: Only in a document with a KiCad board; not while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Insert canvas
commands.summary: Places a picture on a plane in the model, as a reference to trace or compare.
commands.details: Choose the picture, then the plane; a planar face selected first is taken at once. The picture sits on it centred: drag it, type an offset and a width, or snap a corner onto a vertex, then Place. The Canvas panel then opens to move, size and calibrate it.
commands.requires: Not while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Edit canvas
commands.summary: Shows the selected canvas's handles and the Canvas panel, to move, size, turn and set it.
commands.details: Drag the picture to move it, a corner dot to size it ({fixed:shift} frees its proportions) and the knob above it to turn it; or type X, Y, width, height and angle in the panel. The panel also sets its opacity, flips, whether it shows through the model or takes clicks, and its lock. A double-click on a canvas does the same, and each change is one step.
commands.requires: Select a canvas first, or edit one; not while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Calibrate canvas
commands.summary: Scales the canvas so that two points on the picture lie a distance you know apart.
commands.details: Pick two points on the picture, such as the ends of an edge whose length you know, then type their real distance and press {fixed:enter} or Apply. The picture scales about the first point; {fixed:esc} takes back the last point.
commands.requires: Select a canvas first, or edit one; not while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Align canvas to model
commands.summary: Moves, turns and scales the canvas so that two points on the picture land on two points of the model.
commands.details: Pick a point on the picture, then the vertex or circle centre of the model where it belongs, then a second pair. The canvas stays in its plane: model points off it are taken square onto it, and a toast says how far off they were. {fixed:esc} takes back the last pick.
commands.requires: Select a canvas first, or edit one; not while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Trace canvas to sketch
commands.summary: Makes a new sketch on the canvas's plane with the picture's dark shapes as curves.
commands.details: The picture is traced on a worker at the size the canvas has in the model, so calibrate it first. The sketch is named after the canvas, and a toast says how many curves it got.
commands.requires: Select a canvas first, or edit one; not while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Replace canvas picture
commands.summary: Shows another picture in the selected canvas's place.
commands.details: Choose the picture: it keeps the canvas's centre, angle and width, and its height follows the new picture's proportions. It is one step to undo; a linked picture is replaced through its link.
commands.requires: Select a canvas first, or edit one; not while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Close canvas
commands.summary: Ends editing the canvas: its handles and the Canvas panel close.
commands.details: What was changed stays; each change was its own step. OK in the panel and {fixed:esc} do the same.
commands.requires: Only while a canvas is being edited.

commands.title: Backdrop images to canvases
commands.summary: Turns the backdrop pictures of the selected sketch into canvases where they lie.
commands.details: Each picture becomes a canvas in the model with its place and opacity, and leaves the sketch. Canvases can then be moved, calibrated and traced without opening the sketch; it is one step to undo.
commands.requires: Select a sketch that has backdrop pictures; not while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Save
commands.summary: Saves the document; a file in viewer mode becomes an editable OPAD document.
commands.details: A document that has never been saved asks for a file name. Saving appends the new steps to the .opad file, which stays friendly to git and to merges.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Save As
commands.summary: Saves the document under a new file name.
commands.details: The document continues under the new name; the old file stays as it was last saved. Use it to start a variant of a design.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Save as template
commands.summary: Keeps a copy of the document among the templates that New from template offers.
commands.details: The copy goes into the templates folder under the name you give, with an identity of its own. A document made from it starts as an untitled copy, so the template itself never changes.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first (a file in viewer mode cannot be a template until it is saved as OPAD).

commands.title: Export
commands.summary: Writes the selection or the whole design to STEP, STL, OBJ, GLB, DXF, SVG, DWG, PDF or PNG.
commands.details: Choose the format and what to include in the dialog, then where the file goes. Mesh formats are tessellated from the exact shapes; the 2D formats write drawings and sketches, or a 2D view of solids with hidden lines.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Export bill of materials
commands.summary: Writes a parts list of the selection or the whole design to a CSV file.
commands.details: Choose the list (parts only, top level or indented), of the whole document or the selected component, whether masses are listed and in which unit, and the separator; the preview shows the table. Export CSV then asks where the file goes.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Document properties
commands.summary: Edits what every drawing's title block says: title, number, revision, status, owner, project and who designed, checked and approved it.
commands.details: The values are stored in the document as one step, and a sheet can still say otherwise. Add properties of your own and use them in a title block field as =doc:name.
commands.requires: Open an OPAD document; a viewed file is saved as OPAD first.

commands.title: Save screenshot
commands.summary: Saves an image of the 3D view.
commands.details: A dialog asks where to save the PNG. The image is the 3D view as it is now, at its size on screen; panels and chips are left out.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Open file location
commands.summary: Shows the open document's file in the system's file manager.
commands.details: For a file open in viewer mode it is the viewed file. The status bar's path and the browser's document row offer it too.
commands.requires: The document must have a file: save it first.

commands.title: Copy path
commands.summary: Copies the full path of the open document's file to the clipboard.
commands.details: For a file open in viewer mode it is the viewed file. The status bar's path menu also has Copy relative path.
commands.requires: The document must have a file: save it first.

commands.title: Close document
commands.summary: Closes the document and returns to the start screen.
commands.details: If there are unsaved changes you are asked whether to save them. Recent files stay on the start screen.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Quit
commands.summary: Closes OPAD.
commands.details: You are asked about unsaved changes first. Window layout and settings are kept for the next start.

commands.title: Use the ODA File Converter for DWG
commands.summary: Reads and writes DWG through an installed ODA File Converter instead of LibreDWG.
commands.details: The ODA File Converter is third-party software whose licence lets non-members use it for non-commercial purposes only, so turning this on first shows its terms. Off, OPAD converts DWG with LibreDWG's dwg2dxf and dxf2dwg, beside OPAD or on PATH. The choice is kept for the next start.

commands.title: Fit
commands.summary: Zooms to the selection; with nothing selected, to the active component or to everything.
commands.details: The camera keeps its direction and only moves and zooms. While a sketch is open it fits the sketch.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Fit all
commands.summary: Zooms so the whole model fits the view.
commands.details: Unlike Fit, the selection is ignored. While a sketch is open it fits the sketch.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Zoom window
commands.summary: Zooms in on a rectangle you drag around what you want to see.
commands.details: Start it, then drag a box in the view, or click to zoom in around that point; {fixed:esc} cancels. The camera keeps its direction. It is under Fit's arrow, in the View menu and in the view cube's right-click menu.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Previous view
commands.summary: Goes back to the view you had before the last camera move.
commands.details: A view is remembered each time the camera comes to rest, the last 50 of them, and Next view goes forward again. When there is no earlier view the status bar says so. It is under Fit's arrow, in the View menu and in the view cube's right-click menu.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Next view
commands.summary: Goes forward again through the views Previous view stepped back from.
commands.details: A new camera move after stepping back drops the views ahead, as a browser's history does. When there is no later view the status bar says so.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Home
commands.summary: Returns to the document's Home view, or to an isometric view with everything in sight while none is set.
commands.details: Set current view as Home, under the Home button's arrow, in the View menu and in the view cube's right-click menu, keeps the camera in the document. Use it when you lose your way after orbiting. The view cube's house button does the same.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Set current view as Home
commands.summary: Makes the current camera the document's Home view.
commands.details: From then on Home and the view cube's house button return to it, and it is saved with the document; Undo takes it back. It is in the View menu and in the view cube's right-click menu. A file in viewer mode is first saved as an OPAD document or edited as an unsaved copy, as you choose.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Reset Home to the iso view
commands.summary: Drops the document's own Home view, so Home is the isometric view again.
commands.details: Every Home set in the document goes in one step, which Undo takes back. It is available only while the document has a Home of its own, and not in viewer mode; it is in the View menu and in the view cube's right-click menu.
commands.requires: The document needs a Home of its own (Set current view as Home); not available in viewer mode.

commands.title: Align view to plane
commands.summary: Turns the camera to look straight at the sketch plane or at a plane you pick.
commands.details: While sketching it aligns to the sketch at once. Otherwise pick a planar face or an origin plane, and the camera turns square to it.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Turn 90° left
commands.summary: Turns the view 90 degrees to the left about the screen's axis.
commands.details: The model is not moved, only the camera. Use it to stand a drawing or a face upright.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Turn 90° right
commands.summary: Turns the view 90 degrees to the right about the screen's axis.
commands.details: The model is not moved, only the camera. Use it to stand a drawing or a face upright.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Twist view
commands.summary: Turns the view about its own axis by an angle you type.
commands.details: The angle is counter-clockwise, in the angle unit shown, and 0 untwists. Only the camera turns, never the model. It is in the View menu after the 90° turns.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Untwist view
commands.summary: Stands the view upright again, without any twist.
commands.details: Up on screen is the model's Z again (its Y when looking from above or below), or the sketch's own y while a sketch is open. Only the camera turns.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Top view
commands.summary: Looks at the model from above, along -Z.
commands.details: The camera turns smoothly and the model is fitted. The matching face of the view cube does the same.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Front view
commands.summary: Looks at the model from the front, along +Y.
commands.details: The camera turns smoothly and the model is fitted. The matching face of the view cube does the same.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Right view
commands.summary: Looks at the model from the right, along -X.
commands.details: The camera turns smoothly and the model is fitted. The matching face of the view cube does the same.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Isometric view
commands.summary: Looks at the model from a corner, at equal angles to the three axes.
commands.details: The camera turns smoothly and the model is fitted. The view cube's matching corner does the same while its corners turn the view. Not available in 2D mode.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not available in 2D mode.

commands.title: Bottom view
commands.summary: Looks at the model from below, along +Z.
commands.details: The camera turns smoothly and the model is fitted. The matching face of the view cube does the same.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Back view
commands.summary: Looks at the model from the back, along -Y.
commands.details: The camera turns smoothly and the model is fitted. The matching face of the view cube does the same.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Left view
commands.summary: Looks at the model from the left, along +X.
commands.details: The camera turns smoothly and the model is fitted. The matching face of the view cube does the same.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Next region
commands.summary: Moves the keyboard to the next part of the window: ribbon, browser, view, timeline, then each open panel.
commands.details: The part reached is ringed, and its controls take the keys: arrows in the ribbon's tabs, the browser and the timeline, {fixed:tab} in a panel. After the last panel it starts again at the ribbon; a click anywhere takes the ring away.

commands.title: Previous region
commands.summary: Moves the keyboard back to the part of the window before this one.
commands.details: The same round as Next region, the other way: from a panel back to the timeline, the view, the browser and the ribbon. It works from a floating panel too.

commands.title: 2D mode
commands.summary: Locks the view to a plane for drawings: pan and zoom only.
commands.details: Orbiting is off and the grid lies in the viewed plane, following the view so it never ends. Opening a DXF, DWG or SVG for viewing turns it on by itself; the 2D mode chip or this command turns it off.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Layers
commands.summary: Opens the Layers manager of the document's 2D drawings.
commands.details: One row per layer: On, Freeze, Lock, Colour, Linetype, Lineweight and Plot change with a click, each one step to undo, in viewer mode too. Isolate layers, walk through them one at a time, and save layer states with a view.
commands.requires: Only for a document with 2D drawings (DXF, DWG or SVG).

commands.title: Layer walk
commands.summary: Shows the drawings one layer at a time.
commands.details: The walk starts at the current layer of the Layers manager, and its bar steps to the next or the previous layer, off and frozen ones included. Run it again, or close the panel, to see every layer again.
commands.requires: Only for a document with 2D drawings (DXF, DWG or SVG).

commands.title: Isolate layer
commands.summary: Shows only the layers of the selected drawing objects.
commands.details: Select objects on the layers you want, in the view or the browser, and run it. Exit isolate ({key:view.unisolate}) brings the other layers back.
commands.requires: Select drawing objects on the layers first.

commands.title: Object snap
commands.summary: Snaps picked points to the ends, middles, centres, intersections and other points of drawing objects.
commands.details: It applies while measuring and picking points; which kinds it takes are the sketch's snap settings. Its switch is in the status bar beside the other snapping switches.

commands.title: Plot
commands.summary: Plots the 2D drawings to a PDF file or a printer.
commands.details: Choose the area (the drawings' extents, what the view shows, or a window picked in the view), the paper and its orientation, fit or a 1:N scale, monochrome and lineweights. A preview shows the page as it will come out.
commands.requires: Only for a document with 2D drawings.

commands.title: Orthographic
commands.summary: Switches between orthographic and perspective projection.
commands.details: Orthographic keeps parallel edges parallel, which suits measuring and drawings. Perspective looks more natural for presenting a model.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Shaded
commands.summary: Draws bodies shaded, without edge lines.
commands.details: The cleanest look for presenting a design. Picking works as in the other styles.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Shaded + edges
commands.summary: Draws shaded bodies with their edges.
commands.details: The default style: faces and their boundaries are both easy to read. Edges are drawn in the theme's edge colour.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Wireframe
commands.summary: Draws edges only; hidden edges show through.
commands.details: Useful to see inner features and to pick edges behind faces. Faces are not drawn, but clicks still find them.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Hidden line
commands.summary: Draws bodies as line drawings, leaving out the edges hidden behind faces.
commands.details: Faces are filled in the background's colour and their edges and outlines drawn in an ink that stands out against it, so what lies behind a face is hidden, as on a drawing. Drawings (DXF, DWG, SVG) keep their own lines. Hidden edges visible, under its arrow in the View tab, also shows the hidden ones, dashed.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Hidden edges visible
commands.summary: Draws bodies as line drawings, with the hidden edges dashed.
commands.details: As in Hidden line, the faces take the background's colour and hide what is behind them; the edges behind them are drawn as well, dashed and dim, so inner features show. The dashes are built on a worker thread and follow the model as it changes. It is under Hidden line's arrow in the View tab.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Grid
commands.summary: Shows or hides the ground grid.
commands.details: In 3D the grid is a patch under the model, spaced to the model's size; in 2D mode and in sketches it follows the view and its spacing follows the zoom. A fixed spacing set in Grid settings is used everywhere.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Grid settings
commands.summary: Sets the grid spacing, automatic or fixed, and its minimum extent.
commands.details: Automatic spacing follows the zoom in sketches and 2D mode and the model's size in 3D; a fixed spacing is what grid snapping jumps to. The grid is turned on while you change it.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Select through objects
commands.summary: Lets a selection window also pick what is completely hidden behind other bodies, and a click in the Edges or Vertices filter reach edges and points behind faces.
commands.details: Off, a window picks whatever shows inside it, even partly. On, a window drag selects every body inside it, front or back.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: X-ray highlight
commands.summary: Shows the selection and the hover through the bodies in front of them, or lets those bodies hide them.
commands.details: On, as by default, a selected body, face, edge or point and whatever the pointer is over are drawn over everything, so a pick behind another body stays in sight. Off, what is in front hides them, as it hides the bodies themselves. The switch ({key:view.xrayHighlight}) is in the View menu and under the ribbon's Rendering, and Preferences › Display has it too.

commands.title: Hover highlight
commands.summary: Turns the highlight of what the pointer is over on or off.
commands.details: Off, bodies, faces, edges and points no longer light up under the pointer, while a click still picks what is there and the selection is highlighted as before. The view cube and the handles keep their own hover. The switch ({key:view.hoverHighlight}) is in the View menu and under the ribbon's Rendering, and Preferences › Display has it too.

commands.title: Isolate
commands.summary: Shows only the selection until you exit isolation.
commands.details: Everything else is hidden from view, not from the document, and the view frames what is isolated. Exit isolate ({key:view.unisolate}) or the × on the Isolated card in the view brings it back.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Exit isolate
commands.summary: Brings back everything isolation hid.
commands.details: The camera stays where it is. Visibility you set yourself is kept. A click on the Isolated card in the view (its ×) does the same.
commands.requires: Nothing is isolated.

commands.title: Hide others
commands.summary: Hides everything but the selection, in one step.
commands.details: Unlike Isolate, it hides the other objects in the document itself, as Hide does; one Undo brings them all back. Unhide all or the browser's eye shows them again.
commands.requires: Select the objects to keep shown first, in the view or in the browser.

commands.title: Save view
commands.summary: Saves the current camera as a named view.
commands.details: Named views are stored in the document and listed under View > Named views, the first nine with their keys. Tick Also keep which objects are hidden and shown to hide what is hidden now again whenever the view is chosen (everything else is shown); the choice is remembered. A file open in viewer mode asks to become an OPAD document first.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Named view 1
commands.summary: Returns to the first named view in the Named views list.
commands.details: The list numbers the named views in the order they were saved and shows each one's key. A view saved with what was hidden hides that again and shows everything else, in one step that Undo takes back. Without such a view the status bar says how to save one.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Named view 2
commands.summary: Returns to the second named view in the Named views list.
commands.details: The list numbers the named views in the order they were saved and shows each one's key. A view saved with what was hidden hides that again and shows everything else, in one step that Undo takes back. Without such a view the status bar says how to save one.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Named view 3
commands.summary: Returns to the third named view in the Named views list.
commands.details: The list numbers the named views in the order they were saved and shows each one's key. A view saved with what was hidden hides that again and shows everything else, in one step that Undo takes back. Without such a view the status bar says how to save one.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Named view 4
commands.summary: Returns to the fourth named view in the Named views list.
commands.details: The list numbers the named views in the order they were saved and shows each one's key. A view saved with what was hidden hides that again and shows everything else, in one step that Undo takes back. Without such a view the status bar says how to save one.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Named view 5
commands.summary: Returns to the fifth named view in the Named views list.
commands.details: The list numbers the named views in the order they were saved and shows each one's key. A view saved with what was hidden hides that again and shows everything else, in one step that Undo takes back. Without such a view the status bar says how to save one.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Named view 6
commands.summary: Returns to the sixth named view in the Named views list.
commands.details: The list numbers the named views in the order they were saved and shows each one's key. A view saved with what was hidden hides that again and shows everything else, in one step that Undo takes back. Without such a view the status bar says how to save one.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Named view 7
commands.summary: Returns to the seventh named view in the Named views list.
commands.details: The list numbers the named views in the order they were saved and shows each one's key. A view saved with what was hidden hides that again and shows everything else, in one step that Undo takes back. Without such a view the status bar says how to save one.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Named view 8
commands.summary: Returns to the eighth named view in the Named views list.
commands.details: The list numbers the named views in the order they were saved and shows each one's key. A view saved with what was hidden hides that again and shows everything else, in one step that Undo takes back. Without such a view the status bar says how to save one.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Named view 9
commands.summary: Returns to the ninth named view in the Named views list.
commands.details: The list numbers the named views in the order they were saved and shows each one's key. A view saved with what was hidden hides that again and shows everything else, in one step that Undo takes back. Without such a view the status bar says how to save one.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Dark theme
commands.summary: Switches between the dark and the light theme.
commands.details: Every panel, icon and the 3D view follow the theme. The choice is kept for the next start.

commands.title: Extensions
commands.summary: Draws dashed extensions of hovered edges; the cursor snaps onto them and to where two cross.
commands.details: Rest on the end of a line, then move along its direction to follow the dashed line. Works in sketches and while measuring or picking points, drawings included.

commands.title: Tracking
commands.summary: Shows alignment lines through points you hover, along X, Y and Z.
commands.details: Rest on a point to acquire it, then move away: a dashed line appears when the cursor lines up with it. Hold {fixed:shift} to lock onto the line; a tap keeps it locked until {fixed:esc}. With several guides or snaps in reach, a tap shows the next.

commands.title: Grid snapping
commands.summary: Makes placed points jump to grid intersections.
commands.details: Applies to points you click in sketches (hold {fixed:alt} to place one off the grid), when placing a drawing or a sketch's origin, to the point and the base of a box, cylinder or other primitive (on a face, in steps from its corner, as a sketch on that face counts them), and to the distances Move / copy's triad is dragged. Set a fixed spacing in Grid settings for predictable steps.

commands.title: Ortho
commands.summary: Keeps each new line of a sketch horizontal or vertical.
commands.details: The next point lines up with the last one along whichever axis is nearer the cursor. Snaps to points and curves still win; with automatic constraints on, the line gets its horizontal or vertical constraint. Right-click the switch for its settings.

commands.title: Polar
commands.summary: Turns a sketch line's direction in fixed angle steps.
commands.details: Near a multiple of the angle step the line snaps to it. Right-click the switch to choose the step: 5, 10, 15, 22.5, 30, 45 or 90 degrees.

commands.title: View cube edges and corners turn the view
commands.summary: Lets a click on the view cube's edges and corners turn the view, besides its faces.
commands.details: On, an edge shows the view between its two faces and a corner the isometric view from its side. Off, only the six faces react, which are easier to hit on a small cube. The choice is kept for the next start.

commands.title: Hide small parts while navigating
commands.summary: Hides small parts while the view turns, pans or zooms, so that big boards and assemblies move smoothly.
commands.details: Bodies whose longest side is under the small part size (3 mm at first) go out as the camera moves and come back once it has been still for a moment; selected bodies stay. Nothing changes in the model, and the choice is kept for the next session.

commands.title: Small part size
commands.summary: Sets how small a part must be to hide while the view moves, and turns hiding on.
commands.details: Type the size in the length unit you use: bodies whose longest side is under it hide while you orbit, pan and zoom. Hide small parts while navigating turns it off again.

commands.title: Browser
commands.summary: Shows or hides the browser: the document's components, bodies, sketches and drawings.
commands.details: Click a row to select it, use the eye to hide it, and drag rows onto a component to move them. Filter objects ({key:edit.filter}) filters it by name.

commands.title: Annotations
commands.summary: Lists notes, hand drawings and pinned measurements.
commands.details: Filter by author, type and status. Click a card and what its note is pinned to lights up in the view, the face, edge, point or body itself (every pick of a pinned measurement), without changing the selection; a click in the view puts it out. Resolved notes stay in the history.
commands.requires: Open an OPAD document; a file in viewer mode has no annotations.

commands.title: Section panel
commands.summary: Opens the section panel: axis, offset, caps and named sections.
commands.details: Here you choose the cutting axis or a face, type an exact offset and save sections by name; a change made here turns the section on. Dragging the plane's edge in the view does the same.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Timeline
commands.summary: Shows or hides the timeline: every step of the document's history.
commands.details: Each marker is one operation; hover it for who did what and when. Double-click a feature or sketch to edit it.

commands.title: Names on the timeline
commands.summary: Writes each step's name beside its icon on the timeline.
commands.details: Off, the markers show their icons only and the names are in their tooltips. The choice is kept for the next session.

commands.title: Design history only
commands.summary: Keeps the timeline to the steps that make and place geometry.
commands.details: Imports, sketches, features and moves stay; renames, colours, views and sections are left off the timeline, though they stay in the document. The browser's history list follows it.

commands.title: Roll forward to the end
commands.summary: Shows the model with every step again after the timeline was rolled back.
commands.details: Dragging the timeline's marker back shows the model as it was before a step, and a chip over the view says so. This command, or a click on the chip, rolls forward to the end.
commands.requires: Only while the timeline is rolled back.

commands.title: History list in the browser
commands.summary: Lists the timeline's steps in a History folder in the browser.
commands.details: They are listed top to bottom, with the roll-back marker among them. The choice is kept for the next session.

commands.title: Reset layout
commands.summary: Puts the panels and docks back where they started.
commands.details: Floating tool panels return to their default place and size. Use it when a panel got lost off screen.

commands.title: Review workspace
commands.summary: Switches the ribbon to Review: look, measure, mark up, compare and share.
commands.details: Its View, Inspect and Markup tabs never change geometry: measurements, notes and saved views sit beside the model. Compare's version commands do bring changes in (Pull, History's Restore as new changes, Recover documents), and Delete and Rename still work on the selection here. A Design command started here, such as Extrude, switches to Design first. The document and its timeline stay the same and only the ribbon's tabs change; finish an open sketch first.

commands.title: Design workspace
commands.summary: Switches the ribbon to Design: sketches, features, parameters and the assembly.
commands.details: Design is where parts are modelled and arranged. Switching to it returns the selection filter to bodies; a Design command started in another workspace keeps the filter and the faces or edges picked for it.

commands.title: Drawings workspace
commands.summary: Switches to the Drawings workspace: sheets with views, a frame and a title block in the 3D view's place.
commands.details: The sheet shown replaces the 3D view while this workspace is on, and the browser's Drawings folder lists the drawings and their sheets. The document and its timeline stay the same; only the ribbon's tabs and the page change.

commands.title: New drawing
commands.summary: Starts a technical drawing of the model: a sheet with a frame, a title block and standard views.
commands.details: Choose the template and paper, the projection (first or third angle), the scale, the views and their style, of the whole model or the selection; the title block's first fields can be filled in here. The views are laid out on a worker and the Drawings workspace opens on the new sheet.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; a viewed file is saved as OPAD first.

commands.title: New sheet
commands.summary: Adds another sheet to the drawing shown, with its paper, template and scale.
commands.details: The new sheet starts empty: place views on it with Base view. The browser lists the sheets under their drawing in the Drawings folder.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Sheet properties
commands.summary: Edits the sheet shown: its name, paper, template, projection, scale, dimension units and its own title block values.
commands.details: The change is one step. Title block fields left empty are filled in from the sheet, the part and Document properties.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Template from DXF or DWG
commands.summary: Takes the frame and title block of the sheet shown from a DXF or DWG file, such as a company template.
commands.details: The file is read on a worker; its frame replaces the sheet's template and its paper size is taken too. The change is one step.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Title block fields
commands.summary: Places the fields a sheet's template fills in, such as its title, number, scale and who drew it.
commands.details: Drag on the paper to add a field, drag a field to move it and its corner to size it, then choose what it shows, its text height and its alignment; {fixed:del} removes the chosen one. Apply changes the sheet as one step. A sheet without a template asks for one in Sheet properties first.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Base view
commands.summary: Places a front view of the model on the sheet: a frame follows the pointer and a click places it.
commands.details: The other orientations (from the top, right, left, back and below) are on the button's menu. The frame snaps to the other views' centres, and a view dragged later takes the views projected from it along.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Base view from the top
commands.summary: Places a base view of the model seen from the top on the sheet.
commands.details: A frame of the view follows the pointer and a click places it. Base view places the front view; the others are on its menu.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Base view from the right
commands.summary: Places a base view of the model seen from the right on the sheet.
commands.details: A frame of the view follows the pointer and a click places it. Base view places the front view; the others are on its menu.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Base view from the left
commands.summary: Places a base view of the model seen from the left on the sheet.
commands.details: A frame of the view follows the pointer and a click places it. Base view places the front view; the others are on its menu.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Base view from the back
commands.summary: Places a base view of the model seen from the back on the sheet.
commands.details: A frame of the view follows the pointer and a click places it. Base view places the front view; the others are on its menu.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Base view from below
commands.summary: Places a base view of the model seen from below on the sheet.
commands.details: A frame of the view follows the pointer and a click places it. Base view places the front view; the others are on its menu.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Projected view
commands.summary: Adds a view projected from the selected one, on the side the pointer is on.
commands.details: Select one view on the sheet, run it and move to its right, left, top or bottom, or a corner: the new view lines up with it and a click places it. A projected view keeps to its parent's line when either is dragged.
commands.requires: Select one view on the sheet first.

commands.title: Isometric view
commands.summary: Places an isometric view of the model on the sheet.
commands.details: A frame follows the pointer and a click places it. It is a pictorial view, not projected from the others.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Section view
commands.summary: Cuts the selected view along a line you draw and places the cut as a new, hatched view.
commands.details: Click the cutting line's points on the view: two for a full section, more for an offset, half or aligned section; then press {fixed:enter}. The new view follows the pointer on the side it goes, lined up with its parent, and a click places it; type its gap to set it exactly. {fixed:esc} takes back the last point, then leaves.
commands.requires: Select one view on the sheet first.

commands.title: Detail view
commands.summary: Places an enlarged view of a round area of the selected view.
commands.details: Click the centre of the detail, then its radius, then where the detail view goes; it is drawn at twice the parent's scale, or the next standard scale up when that is not one. Type the radius, or a scale such as 5:1, to set them exactly. {fixed:esc} takes back the last step.
commands.requires: Select one view on the sheet first.

commands.title: Auxiliary view
commands.summary: Places a view that looks square to a slanted edge of the selected view, so an inclined face shows at its true shape.
commands.details: Click a straight edge of the view, then move to the side the new view goes and click to place it, lined up along that edge. Type its gap to set it exactly; {fixed:esc} steps back.
commands.requires: Select one view on the sheet first.

commands.title: Broken-out section
commands.summary: Cuts away part of the selected view, inside an outline you draw, to show what is inside.
commands.details: Click points round what to open up (a smooth closed curve goes through them) and press {fixed:enter}. Then click a point in a view beside it to set how deep the cut goes, or press {fixed:enter} again for the part's middle. It works on base, projected and auxiliary views.
commands.requires: Select one view on the sheet first.

commands.title: Crop view
commands.summary: Keeps only the part of the selected view inside a box.
commands.details: Drag a box around the part to keep, or click its two corners; type its width and height to set them exactly. The rest of the view is left out, and the change is one step.
commands.requires: Select one view on the sheet first.

commands.title: Break view
commands.summary: Shortens a long view by taking out the band between two points.
commands.details: Click where the break starts and where it ends: the band between them is taken out in the direction they lie farther apart (sideways or up and down), and zigzag break lines mark where the halves meet. Type its length to set it exactly; the change is one step.
commands.requires: Select one view on the sheet first.

commands.title: Hidden lines
commands.summary: Shows or hides dashed hidden lines in the selected views, or in every view of the sheet.
commands.details: It changes the views' style as one step. With no view selected it applies to the whole sheet.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Tangent edges
commands.summary: Draws the edges where faces meet smoothly as thin lines, or leaves them out.
commands.details: It changes the selected views' style, or every view's when none is selected, as one step. A view's right-click menu also draws them as ordinary edges.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Update views
commands.summary: Projects the sheet's views again from the model as it is now.
commands.details: The views are projected on a worker; until each is ready its old drawing stays, marked Updating. Nothing in the document changes.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Fit sheet
commands.summary: Zooms the sheet so all of it shows.
commands.details: It changes only how the sheet is shown, never the drawing. The wheel zooms about the pointer and a middle drag pans.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Export sheet
commands.summary: Writes the sheet shown to PDF, SVG, DXF, DWG or PNG.
commands.details: Choose the file and its type; it is written on a worker. A drawing with several sheets goes into one PDF from its row in the browser's Drawings folder.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Export drawing as PDF
commands.summary: Writes every sheet of the drawing shown into one PDF, a page per sheet.
commands.details: Choose where the file goes; it is written on a worker. Export sheet writes the sheet shown alone, also as SVG, DXF, DWG or PNG.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Print
commands.summary: Prints the drawing's sheets, with a preview of each page.
commands.details: Choose the printer, all sheets of the drawing or this one, fit to the printer's paper or actual size, black ink only and the copies. The sheets are drawn on a worker, and a toast says when they have gone to the printer.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Issue revision
commands.summary: Releases the drawing as a revision: its values and views as they are now are kept, and the revision table and title block show it.
commands.details: Set the revision, its description and date and who issued and approved it; you can also keep the views' linework in the document, write the issued PDF and commit and tag it in git. Afterwards the chip over the sheet says when the drawing has changed since that revision.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Dimension
commands.summary: Adds a dimension to a view: pick what to measure and click where it goes.
commands.details: Pick an edge, a circle or a point, and a second one for a distance or an angle; where the pointer is chooses horizontal, vertical, aligned, angle, radius or diameter. Click to place it, or type its offset, decimals or tolerance in the boxes beside the pointer and press {fixed:enter}. The bar under the sheet sets its type, precision, tolerance and text; {fixed:esc} takes back a pick, then leaves.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Ordinate dimensions
commands.summary: Measures several features of a view from one origin, as a row of values on extension lines.
commands.details: Pick the origin (a datum edge, a vertex or a centre), then the features to measure from it, then press {fixed:enter} or Done and click where the dimensions go. The side of the view the pointer is on chooses horizontal or vertical values, unless Direction in the bar says otherwise; the set is one step.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Baseline dimensions
commands.summary: Measures several features of a view from one origin, as a stack of dimensions that all start there.
commands.details: Pick the origin (a datum edge, a vertex or a centre), then the features to measure from it, then press {fixed:enter} or Done and click where the dimensions go. The side of the view the pointer is on chooses horizontal or vertical values, unless Direction in the bar says otherwise; the set is one step.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Chain dimensions
commands.summary: Measures several features of a view one after the other, each dimension starting where the last one ends.
commands.details: Pick the origin (a datum edge, a vertex or a centre), then the features to measure from it, then press {fixed:enter} or Done and click where the dimensions go. The side of the view the pointer is on chooses horizontal or vertical values, unless Direction in the bar says otherwise; the set is one step.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Dimension from datums
commands.summary: Dimensions the holes of a view from its datum symbols in one go, as ordinate dimensions.
commands.details: Place two datum symbols on straight edges of the view first, one upright and one level. The selected view, or the first one with datum symbols, then gets a set of ordinate dimensions per direction, measured on a worker and added as one step. The button's menu has baseline and chain dimensions instead.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Baseline dimensions from datums
commands.summary: Dimensions the holes of a view from its datum symbols in one go, as baseline dimensions.
commands.details: Place two datum symbols on straight edges of the view first, one upright and one level. The selected view, or the first one with datum symbols, then gets a set of baseline dimensions per direction, measured on a worker and added as one step.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Chain dimensions from datums
commands.summary: Dimensions the holes of a view from its datum symbols in one go, as chain dimensions.
commands.details: Place two datum symbols on straight edges of the view first, one upright and one level. The selected view, or the first one with datum symbols, then gets a set of chain dimensions per direction, measured on a worker and added as one step.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Hole callout
commands.summary: Labels a hole with its size and depth, read from the model.
commands.details: Pick the hole by its circle or its wall; the callout follows the pointer on a leader, and a click places it. It writes the diameter and depth (or THRU), a counterbore or countersink, and how many holes of that size the part has (2×).
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Hole table
commands.summary: Lists the holes of a view in a table: a tag for each, its X and Y position and its size.
commands.details: Click the view whose holes go in, then where the table's top left corner goes. Each hole gets its tag on the view, lettered by size (A1, A2, B1), and its row in the table.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Centre mark
commands.summary: Marks the centre of a circle on a view with a cross.
commands.details: Pick a circle seen along its axis: the mark is added at once, each one a step. The tool stays on for the next circle; {fixed:esc} leaves.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Centre line
commands.summary: Draws a centre line along a cylinder seen from the side, between two circles or between two parallel edges.
commands.details: Pick a cylinder seen from the side and the line is added at once; or pick two circles or two parallel edges, and it is added after the second. The tool stays on for the next one; {fixed:esc} leaves.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Centre marks on views
commands.summary: Draws centre marks on every circle of the selected views, or of every view of the sheet, or takes them off.
commands.details: The views draw the marks themselves, so they follow the model. The change to the views' style is one step.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Note
commands.summary: Adds a text note to the sheet, with a leader to what it points at when you pick that first.
commands.details: Type the text in the bar under the sheet, then click where the note goes; for a leader, pick an edge, a circle or a point first. A note placed inside a view belongs to that view and moves with it.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Datum
commands.summary: Places a datum symbol, a lettered frame on a triangle, on an edge of a view.
commands.details: Pick the edge the datum stands on; the frame follows the pointer and a click places it. It takes the next free letter, which the bar under the sheet can change; the datums then serve Dimension from datums and feature control frames.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Feature control frame
commands.summary: Adds a geometric tolerance frame: the characteristic, the tolerance and its datums.
commands.details: Set the characteristic (position, flatness, perpendicularity and the others), the value, a diameter zone, the material modifier and the datum letters in the bar under the sheet. Pick the feature it controls and click where the frame goes, or click a view without picking for a frame without a leader.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Surface texture
commands.summary: Places a surface texture symbol on an edge, with its roughness value.
commands.details: Pick the edge of the surface, then click on the side the symbol stands, along the edge. The bar under the sheet sets the process (material removal required, any process, or no material removal) and the value, such as Ra 1.6.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Parts list
commands.summary: Places the drawing's parts list on the sheet: item, quantity, name, part number and material.
commands.details: The table follows the pointer by its bottom right corner and a click places it. The bar under the sheet lists the top level or every part once with its quantity, and can add a Mass column; balloons take their numbers from it.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Balloon
commands.summary: Labels a part on a view with its item number from the parts list.
commands.details: Pick an edge of the part, then click where the balloon goes; its number comes from the parts list. Quantity in the bar under the sheet also writes how many there are (4×).
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Auto-balloon
commands.summary: Balloons every part a view shows that has no balloon yet, spread around the view.
commands.details: It takes the selected view, else an isometric view, else the first base view. The balloons are placed in columns and rows so that none overlap, and a parts list is added when the drawing has none; all of it is one step.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Revision table
commands.summary: Places the drawing's revision table: each issued revision with its description, date and approval.
commands.details: The table follows the pointer by its top right corner and a click places it. Its rows come from Issue revision, so it grows as revisions are issued.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Re-attach
commands.summary: Gives an annotation that lost what it measures new references, picked on its view.
commands.details: Select the annotation, or open the sheet's dangling chip, which lists the ones that lost theirs, and choose it there. Then pick as many edges, circles or points as it had, on its own view: it measures again, and the change is one step.
commands.requires: Select one annotation on the sheet first.

commands.title: Navigation: Fusion-style
commands.summary: Uses Fusion-style mouse buttons for orbit, pan and zoom.
commands.details: Pick the preset your hands already know; it changes only the mouse buttons, not the keyboard shortcuts. In every preset scrolling zooms at the pointer as a mouse wheel does; on a trackpad, answer Trackpad pans when the first scroll asks (or choose it in Preferences › Keyboard and mouse › Scroll wheel / trackpad) and two fingers pan, {fixed:shift} with them orbits. On macOS a trackpad pans without asking. The choice is kept for the next start.

commands.title: Navigation: SOLIDWORKS-style
commands.summary: Uses SOLIDWORKS-style mouse buttons for orbit, pan and zoom.
commands.details: Pick the preset your hands already know; it changes only the mouse buttons, not the keyboard shortcuts. In every preset scrolling zooms at the pointer as a mouse wheel does; on a trackpad, answer Trackpad pans when the first scroll asks (or choose it in Preferences › Keyboard and mouse › Scroll wheel / trackpad) and two fingers pan, {fixed:shift} with them orbits. On macOS a trackpad pans without asking. The choice is kept for the next start.

commands.title: Navigation: Onshape-style
commands.summary: Uses Onshape-style mouse buttons for orbit, pan and zoom.
commands.details: Pick the preset your hands already know; it changes only the mouse buttons, not the keyboard shortcuts. In every preset scrolling zooms at the pointer as a mouse wheel does; on a trackpad, answer Trackpad pans when the first scroll asks (or choose it in Preferences › Keyboard and mouse › Scroll wheel / trackpad) and two fingers pan, {fixed:shift} with them orbits. On macOS a trackpad pans without asking. The choice is kept for the next start.

commands.title: Navigation: Blender-style
commands.summary: Uses Blender-style mouse buttons for orbit, pan and zoom.
commands.details: Pick the preset your hands already know; it changes only the mouse buttons, not the keyboard shortcuts. In every preset scrolling zooms at the pointer as a mouse wheel does; on a trackpad, answer Trackpad pans when the first scroll asks (or choose it in Preferences › Keyboard and mouse › Scroll wheel / trackpad) and two fingers pan, {fixed:shift} with them orbits. On macOS a trackpad pans without asking. The choice is kept for the next start.

commands.title: Navigation: CAD 2D
commands.summary: Uses drafting mouse buttons: the middle button pans, the wheel zooms and nothing orbits.
commands.details: {fixed:ctrl} with the middle button zooms as well, and {fixed:shift} with a trackpad pans instead of orbiting. It changes only the mouse, not the keyboard shortcuts. Scrolling zooms as a mouse wheel does until Trackpad pans is chosen (the first scroll asks; Preferences › Keyboard and mouse › Scroll wheel / trackpad changes it); on macOS a trackpad pans without asking. The choice is kept for the next start.

commands.title: Animate view changes
commands.summary: Turns the camera smoothly to a new view instead of jumping there.
commands.details: It applies to the standard views, Home, Fit, Previous and Next view, the zoom window and the turns. Off, the camera jumps straight to the new view, as it also does while Reduce motion is on in Preferences › Display. The choice is kept for the next start.

commands.title: Lower quality while navigating
commands.summary: Draws a model that is slow to draw with less detail while the view moves.
commands.details: When a full frame takes longer than about 20 ms, shadows, outlines and extra resolution are left out while you orbit, pan or zoom, and the full image is back a moment after the view rests. Off, every frame is drawn in full, however slow. The choice is kept for the next start.

commands.title: Bodies
commands.summary: Makes a click pick whole bodies.
commands.details: The hover highlight shows what a click would pick. The default for Design; Review measures pick what the tool needs.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; while sketching, the sketch decides what a click picks.

commands.title: Faces
commands.summary: Makes a click pick faces of bodies.
commands.details: The hover highlight shows what a click would pick. Faces are what you measure, sketch on and press-pull.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; while sketching, the sketch decides what a click picks.

commands.title: Edges
commands.summary: Makes a click pick edges, and the lines and curves of drawings.
commands.details: The hover highlight shows what a click would pick. Edges are what fillets and chamfers work on.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; while sketching, the sketch decides what a click picks.

commands.title: Vertices
commands.summary: Makes a click pick vertices, the corner points of bodies.
commands.details: The hover highlight shows what a click would pick. Vertices are handy as exact points for measuring.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; while sketching, the sketch decides what a click picks.

commands.title: Distance
commands.summary: Measures the distance between two picks: the shortest, centre to centre or the largest.
commands.details: Pick two faces, edges, vertices or bodies; the result shows the distance, its X, Y and Z parts and the measured points. Started from the Bodies filter it picks faces until it ends: select bodies first, or choose Bodies while it runs, to measure whole bodies. Minimum, Centre to centre and Maximum in the panel choose which distance. A dashed preview line follows the cursor after the first pick, and Pin ({key:inspect.pin}) keeps the result in the document.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Angle
commands.summary: Measures the angle between two faces or edges.
commands.details: Pick the first face or edge, then the second. The result shows the angle and its supplement.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Radius
commands.summary: Measures the radius and diameter of a circular edge or a cylindrical face.
commands.details: Pick one round face, or a circular edge with the Edges filter. The result shows R and Ø; Pin ({key:inspect.pin}) keeps it in the document.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Bounding box
commands.summary: Draws the world-aligned box around the picks and reports its size.
commands.details: Each click adds what the selection filter picks, a body, face, edge or vertex, and the box grows to hold them all; {fixed:esc} takes the last one back. The box is measured tightly on a worker thread, so large parts do not freeze the view.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Area
commands.summary: Measures the area and perimeter enclosed by picked faces, edges or drawing objects, or by picked points.
commands.details: Each pick adds to the boundary: faces give their exact area, edges and objects the loops they close (a loop inside another is a hole), three points or more the polygon through them. One object that encloses nothing alone grows into the smallest area around the clicked part; while the picks enclose nothing the panel says what is still open. Pin ({key:inspect.pin}) keeps the result in the document.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Length and area
commands.summary: Measures an edge's length, a face's area or a body's surface area.
commands.details: Pick one edge, face or body. An edge gives its length along the curve and the perimeter of each face loop it belongs to; a face its area and perimeters; a body its surface area, and its volume when it is a solid. From the Vertices filter it picks edges while it runs.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Interference
commands.summary: Finds bodies that overlap or nearly touch and lists each pair.
commands.details: It runs as the panel opens, on the selected bodies or on all solids when nothing is selected, and again whenever the model changes; a Clearance above 0 also lists pairs closer than it. Click a row and the pair is selected: an overlap shows in red over them, a pair that is only close shows its gap as a dimension. Keep as check then opens it in Design as an Interference check feature with the same bodies and clearance; OK adds it to the history, where it runs again whenever those bodies change.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Print check
commands.summary: Checks a part for 3D printing: overhangs, build-plate contact and thin walls.
commands.details: Works on solids and on meshes such as STL and 3MF. It runs as the panel opens and again whenever the model changes, and lists each finding; on the part overhangs turn amber and thin walls red, seen through the model like a selection, until the panel closes. A clicked finding is selected.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Pin
commands.summary: Keeps the current measurement in the document as an annotation.
commands.details: A pinned measurement stays visible, appears in the Annotations panel and is part of the history. Remove it there when it is no longer needed.
commands.requires: Measure something first with Distance, Angle, Radius or Bounding box.

commands.title: Clear measurement
commands.summary: Steps back one level: closes a popup or panel, cancels a pick, leaves a tool or clears the measurement.
commands.details: {fixed:esc} always undoes the most recent thing first. Press it again to keep stepping back until nothing is left.

commands.title: Properties
commands.summary: Shows the properties of the selection: name, id, volume, area and size.
commands.details: Names and ids show at once; volume, area and the exact box are measured in the background and fill in. Pin the panel to make it follow the selection.
commands.requires: Select the objects first, in the view or in the browser.

commands.title: Part properties
commands.summary: Gives the selected bodies or components a part number, description, material, density or mass, vendor and notes.
commands.details: The fields feed the bill of materials and the drawings' title blocks, and a material from the library gives the mass from the volume. Several objects are edited at once, as one step, and Properties shows the result in its Part section.
commands.requires: Select bodies or components first.

commands.title: Material
commands.summary: Gives the selected bodies or components a material from the library.
commands.details: Choose it from the menu, which lists each material with its density: the mass then follows from the volume, and with Colour as the material on they take its colour too. It is one step to undo; None clears it, and Other material… opens Part properties.
