commands.requires: Select bodies or components first; not while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Select similar
commands.summary: Selects every face or edge like the picked one: the same hole, fillet radius or direction; for a body picked whole, a rule.
commands.details: Pick a face or an edge of a solid, then Select similar: the matches are found on a worker and selected at once; run it again for the next rule. On a body picked whole it starts with the top perimeter, then the bottom perimeter, edges along X, Y or Z, circular edges, upward faces, holes, fillets and chamfers. Useful to pick every hole at once for a fillet.
commands.requires: Pick a face or an edge of a solid, or a body, first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Section
commands.summary: Cuts the view with a plane to look inside; drag the plane's edge to move it.
commands.details: Only the view is cut, never the model. Cut faces get caps so solids read as solid, and the Section panel holds exact offsets and named sections.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Flip section
commands.summary: Shows the other side of the section.
commands.details: The cutting plane stays where it is; the kept half swaps. Turn Section on first.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Note
commands.summary: Pins a text note to a body, face, edge or point.
commands.details: Click the target (the selection filter decides whether that is a body, face, edge or point), type the note and save it with {fixed:ctrlEnter}. Notes keep their author and time, and live in the document's history.
commands.requires: Open an OPAD document, and finish the sketch first.

commands.title: Hand drawing
commands.summary: Draws freehand strokes on the model.
commands.details: Pick a target, then drag to draw; each stroke lies on a plane facing the camera, so it stays in place when you orbit. Save keeps the drawing as one annotation.
commands.requires: Open an OPAD document, and finish the sketch first.

commands.title: Resolve note
commands.summary: Marks the selected note as resolved.
commands.details: A resolved note leaves the view and is dimmed in the Annotations panel, where Restore brings it back; it stays in the history, so the discussion is never lost. Filter the panel by status to hide them.
commands.requires: Select a note in the Annotations panel first.

commands.title: Show notes
commands.summary: Shows or hides note cards in the 3D view.
commands.details: Hiding them only declutters the view. The notes stay in the document and in the Annotations panel.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Undo
commands.summary: Undoes the last change.
commands.details: In a sketch it undoes the last sketch edit; in the note editor the last stroke. Undo history keeps the last 50 steps by default.
commands.requires: Nothing to undo.

commands.title: Redo
commands.summary: Redoes the change you just undid.
commands.details: Redo is available until you make a new change. In a sketch it redoes sketch edits.
commands.requires: Nothing to redo.

commands.title: Cut
commands.summary: Copies the selection and then deletes it, as Delete does.
commands.details: Paste ({key:edit.paste}) puts it back, here or in another OPAD window; in a sketch it cuts the selected curves. Undo brings the originals back.

commands.title: Copy
commands.summary: Copies the selected bodies and components, or in a sketch the selected curves with the constraints among them.
commands.details: Paste ({key:edit.paste}) then makes copies, also in another OPAD window. With nothing selected, the current timeline marker's operation id is copied instead.

commands.title: Paste
commands.summary: Places what was copied: bodies as new bodies, sketch curves in the open sketch.
commands.details: In the document they came from, the copies start beside the originals in a Move / copy panel, and {fixed:enter} makes them; from another document they are imported as they were. In a sketch the curves follow the pointer by their base point until a click places them.

commands.title: Paste as linked instances
commands.summary: Puts the copied parts in again as instances of the same stored bodies.
commands.details: The instances use the bodies the originals use rather than copies of them, and the Linked instances panel lists them. It is one undo step.

commands.title: Repeat
commands.summary: Runs the last tool, feature, check or edit again.
commands.details: The menu entry names the command it repeats, and it is the first entry of the view's context menu. {fixed:enter} in the view repeats it too while nothing runs, except Delete, Restore, Hide and Show all, which repeat only from here. View navigation, file open and save, panel toggles and plain selection commands are not repeated; Import, Export, Screenshot, Isolate, Save view and Select similar are.

commands.title: Select all
commands.summary: Selects every body on screen, or every curve of the sketch being edited.
commands.details: Hidden bodies and those outside an isolation stay out. In a face, edge or vertex filter the view goes back to bodies first; while a tool or a feature input is picking, nothing changes.

commands.title: Invert selection
commands.summary: Selects the bodies on screen that are not selected, and lets go of those that are.
commands.details: In a sketch it swaps the selected and unselected curves. Use it to pick everything but a few parts: select those, then invert.

commands.title: Rename
commands.summary: Renames the selection; several objects are numbered where {n} stands.
commands.details: One object is renamed in place in the browser. For several, type a name such as Leg {n} and they become Leg 1, Leg 2 and so on, in selection order.
commands.requires: Select the objects first, in the view or in the browser.

commands.title: Hide
commands.summary: Hides the selection.
commands.details: Hidden objects stay in the document; the browser's eye shows them again. Unhide all ({key:edit.showall}) brings back everything.
commands.requires: Select the objects first, in the view or in the browser.

commands.title: Unhide all
commands.summary: Shows everything that is hidden.
commands.details: Bodies, components and sketches you hid become visible again. Isolation is separate: leave it with Exit isolate.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Filter objects
commands.summary: Opens the browser and puts the cursor in its name filter.
commands.details: Type part of a name to narrow the browser to matching rows. Clear the field to see everything again.

commands.title: Select parent
commands.summary: Selects the component that contains the selection.
commands.details: Press it again to climb further up the assembly. Useful after clicking a single body deep inside an imported model.
commands.requires: Select the objects first, in the view or in the browser.

commands.title: Select less
commands.summary: Steps the selection back down what Select parent climbed.
commands.details: From a feature's faces back to the faces picked first, from a component to its body. Select parent ({key:edit.selectparent}) climbs up again.

commands.title: Related selections
commands.summary: Lists what the picked faces or edges belong to, with what can be done to it.
commands.details: The feature that made them, a hole, a fillet chain or a loop: pick one to select it, or delete, edit or suppress it, or find it in the timeline. The smart chip's ▾ opens the same list.

commands.title: Suggest related selections
commands.summary: Shows a chip beside picked faces or edges naming what they belong to.
commands.details: A click on the chip, or Select parent ({key:edit.selectparent}), selects that whole feature or detail, and on such a selection the chip carries its actions. Off, the chip comes only with Select parent, Related selections or Delete.

commands.title: Delete
commands.summary: Removes the selection; the history keeps it restorable.
commands.details: In a design the bodies leave through a Remove step at the end of the timeline; a sketch, or a whole import in an imported model, is tombstoned by a delete step. Undo brings them back, and so does Restore ({key:edit.restore}) on that Remove or delete step.
commands.requires: Select the objects first, in the view or in the browser.

commands.title: Restore
commands.summary: Brings back what a delete or Remove step took out.
commands.details: Select the delete or Remove step on the timeline first; on a tombstoned (dashed) marker it brings that step back. The restore is a new step, so it can itself be undone.
commands.requires: Select a delete or Remove step on the timeline first.

commands.title: Select what it touches
commands.summary: Selects the objects the current timeline step changed.
commands.details: Clicking a marker on the timeline already selects what the step made. Select what it touches ({key:edit.selecttouched}) then takes the whole bodies or components it changed, in the view and the browser.
commands.requires: Click a marker on the timeline first.

commands.title: Search commands
commands.summary: Finds any command by typing part of its name.
commands.details: Use the arrow keys and {fixed:enter} to run the command. Every command of the menus and the ribbon is listed with its shortcut.

commands.title: Keyboard shortcuts
commands.summary: Shows every shortcut and lets you change them.
commands.details: Search by name or press the keys to find what they do. Conflicts are flagged before you save, and Restore default puts a command back to its default.

commands.title: Annotation author
commands.summary: Sets the name recorded on your notes and changes.
commands.details: The name appears on note cards and in the timeline's tooltips. It defaults to your system user name (GIT_AUTHOR_NAME or OPAD_AUTHOR when set).

commands.title: Undo history
commands.summary: Sets how many steps Undo keeps.
commands.details: The default is 50, the range 1 to 1000. Older steps stay in the document's history; only undo forgets them.

commands.title: Clear tessellation cache
commands.summary: Deletes OPAD's user cache: display meshes and the remembered copies of slow files.
commands.details: The cache makes large files open faster the second time. Clearing it frees disk space; the next open is slower once.

commands.title: Settings
commands.summary: Opens the settings menu: Preferences, keyboard shortcuts, the theme, the navigation preset and the panels, then Recover documents and Agent activity.
commands.details: Everything that is set once lives in Preferences; this menu keeps the switches used every day. Every setting is kept for the next start.

commands.title: Preferences
commands.summary: Shows every setting of OPAD in one window, with a search.
commands.details: Pages for display, units and precision, sketch snaps, the grid, files, autosave, version control, keyboard and mouse, and AI access. Type in the search field to keep only the pages and rows that match. Changes apply at once and are kept for the next start.

commands.title: Help for this tool
commands.summary: Opens the guide of the tool you are using: what it does, its keys and its animated steps.
commands.details: With no tool running it opens the tool guide where you left it. Over a ribbon button or a menu entry, its key ({key:help.current}) expands that command's card instead.

commands.title: Tool guide
commands.summary: The commands, each with what it does, its current keys and, for most, an animated guide; searchable.
commands.details: Search by name or by what you want to do; pick a command to see its card and its clip, and click a step to loop it. A command not available now says what it needs.

commands.title: Shortcuts cheat sheet
commands.summary: Lists every keyboard shortcut and mouse gesture at a glance.
commands.details: The keys are grouped as in the command search, with the mouse of your navigation preset and the keys every tool knows. Search by name or key; Change shortcuts opens the editor, and {fixed:esc}, or the key that opened it ({key:help.shortcuts}) while nothing is typed in the search, closes the sheet.

commands.title: Getting started
commands.summary: Six short animated lessons: move around, open, measure, sketch, make a solid and find any command.
commands.details: Each lesson shows its clip; all but the first have a Try it button that runs the command it teaches. The navigation lesson follows your mouse preset, and every key shown is your current one.

commands.title: Report a problem
commands.summary: Writes a problem report with what happened and the facts about OPAD and this computer.
commands.details: Nothing is sent by itself: copy the report or save it as a text file, or open the issue page and paste it there. The report names the document's kind and size, never its path or name.

commands.title: Third-party licences
commands.summary: Lists the libraries OPAD is built on, with their versions, sources and licence texts.
commands.details: OPAD itself is under the MIT licence; every library keeps its own. About Qt in the same window shows Qt's terms, and opad-cli licenses prints the same text.

commands.title: About Qt
commands.summary: Shows the version of Qt that OPAD runs on and Qt's licence.
commands.details: OPAD's windows, menus and panels are made with Qt, used under the LGPL version 3. The other libraries are listed under Third-party licences.

commands.title: About OPAD
commands.summary: Shows the OPAD version, its licence and the libraries it is built on.
commands.details: OPAD is free software under the MIT licence, built on Open CASCADE Technology, Qt and other libraries, each under its own licence. It has headless twins: opad-cli on the command line and the opad Python module. Both read and write the same documents.

commands.title: New sketch
commands.summary: Starts a sketch on an origin plane, a planar face or a construction plane.
commands.details: Click an origin plane (in the view or the corner tiles), a planar face, a construction plane or a sketch: the camera turns square to it. Place the origin or keep it and press OK; the ribbon switches to the Sketch tools. Finish sketch keeps the result as one step on the timeline.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Drawing to sketch
commands.summary: Turns an imported 2D drawing into an editable sketch in the drawing's own plane.
commands.details: Choose the layers to bring in; lines, arcs and circles become sketch curves you can constrain and extrude. The drawing itself stays as it was. Tick Construction only for helper layers such as centre lines. The curves come in unconstrained.
commands.requires: Open or create a document with an imported drawing (DXF, DWG or SVG) first.

commands.title: Parameters
commands.summary: Named values usable in any dimension or feature field.
commands.details: Define width = 40 mm once and type width, or an expression such as width / 2, wherever a value is asked. Changing a parameter regenerates everything that uses it.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Regenerate
commands.summary: Recomputes every feature from the start of the timeline.
commands.details: Normally only what changed is recomputed. Use it after updating an imported file or to check that the whole history still builds.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Edit feature
commands.summary: Edits the feature or sketch selected on the timeline.
commands.details: The timeline rolls back to that step, so later steps are dimmed while you edit. OK regenerates everything after it.
commands.requires: Select a feature or a sketch on the timeline first, or double-click it.

commands.title: New component
commands.summary: Adds a component, named Component N, in the active component or the selected one.
commands.details: It becomes the active component, so what you make next goes into it (the Activate box under its name, or Activate new components, changes that), and its name is ready to type in the browser. Drag bodies onto it in the browser, or use Move to component.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Move to component
commands.summary: Moves the selection under another component, keeping it where it is.
commands.details: A list opens at the pointer with the document root and every component the selection can go to; type to narrow it, then click one or press {fixed:enter}. What moves keeps its place in the world, as one step.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Component from selection
commands.summary: Puts the selected bodies and components into a new component, where they are.
commands.details: The new component is made in their nearest common component, in one step, and its name is ready to type in the browser. What moves into it keeps its place in the world.
commands.requires: Select bodies or components first; not while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Activate new components
commands.summary: Makes each new component the active one as it is made.
commands.details: On, what you make after New component goes into it; off, the active component stays as it was. The Activate box under a new component's name changes this too.

commands.title: Activate component
commands.summary: Makes a component the active one: new sketches, features, bodies and imports go into it.
commands.details: Select a component, or a body in it, and run it; the radio button on a browser row does the same, and so does a double-click on a ghost. The rest of the model is ghosted, and the chip over the view names the active component: a click on it activates the document root again.
commands.requires: Select a component, or a body in it, that is not active yet.

commands.title: Activate root
commands.summary: Makes the document root active again, so nothing is ghosted.
commands.details: New sketches, features and bodies then go to the top of the document. A click on the active component's chip does the same.
commands.requires: Only while a component is active.

commands.title: Active component visibility
commands.summary: Chooses whether the rest of the model is ghosted while a component is active.
commands.details: On, everything outside the active component is drawn faintly and picked only as a reference; off, it is drawn and picked as it is. Inactive opacity, beside it in the Design menu and the chip's right-click menu, sets how faint the ghosts are.

commands.title: Only the active component's history
commands.summary: Keeps the timeline to the steps that touch the active component.
commands.details: Off, the other steps stay on the timeline, dimmed. It matters only while a component is active.

commands.title: Exploded view
commands.summary: Moves the parts of the assembly apart in the view, to show how it goes together.
commands.details: The Explode panel sets the level, the distance (a slider, with Play), the layout and what moves together; dashed lines show where each part belongs. Only the view changes, never the model, and Save exploded view keeps the arrangement as a named view.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Play explode
commands.summary: Moves the parts out, or back together when they are out.
commands.details: It animates the exploded view's distance. {fixed:space} does the same in the Explode panel.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Collapse exploded view
commands.summary: Puts the parts back where the model has them.
commands.details: The exploded view's settings are kept, so Exploded view opens it again as it was. Saved exploded views do not change.
commands.requires: Only while the view is exploded.

commands.title: Save exploded view
commands.summary: Keeps the exploded arrangement as a named view in the document.
commands.details: Name it; choosing it later under View > Named views, or in the Explode panel, explodes the view again. A file open in viewer mode asks to become an OPAD document first.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Keep together
commands.summary: Makes the selected component move as one part in the exploded view, at any level.
commands.details: Use it for a subassembly that stays whole, such as a circuit board with its parts. The component's badge in the browser shows the rule, and a click on it switches the rule.
commands.requires: Only while the view is exploded, with a component selected.

commands.title: Explode its parts
commands.summary: Moves the selected component's parts apart in the exploded view, whatever the level.
commands.details: Use it for a folder of screws inside a part that is kept whole. Turn it off to let the component follow the level again.
commands.requires: Only while the view is exploded, with a component selected.

commands.title: Group (explode as one)
commands.summary: Makes the selected bodies and components move as one in the exploded view.
commands.details: The browser marks what moves together, and a saved exploded view keeps the group. Ungroup lets them move on their own again.
commands.requires: Only while the view is exploded, with two or more objects selected.

commands.title: Ungroup
commands.summary: Lets the selected objects of an explode group move on their own again.
commands.details: Only the exploded view changes. The browser stops marking them as moving together.
commands.requires: Only while the view is exploded, with a grouped object selected.

commands.title: Colour
commands.summary: Sets the colour of the selection.
commands.details: Pick the colour in the dialog; every selected object gets it, as one step. In viewer mode it is a view setting and is not saved.
commands.requires: Select the objects first, in the view or in the browser.

commands.title: Opacity
commands.summary: Makes the selection see-through, from 10 to 100 percent.
commands.details: A slider opens at the pointer (and in the right-click menu): the view follows it, and letting go keeps it as one step. Lower opacity lets you see parts inside a housing; picking still works on see-through bodies.
commands.requires: Select the objects first, in the view or in the browser.

commands.title: Lock
commands.summary: Locks the selection against picking and edits, or unlocks it.
commands.details: Locked objects stay visible but the hover no longer finds them, so you can work on what is in front or around. Use it again to unlock.
commands.requires: Select the objects first, in the view or in the browser.

commands.title: Box
commands.summary: A box on a plane at a position, sized by length, width and height.
commands.details: Click a plane or a planar face where it goes, move the pointer to draw the base and click (or type its length, {fixed:tab}, its width, then {fixed:enter} or {fixed:tab}), then drag the arrow or type the height; {fixed:enter} adds it and {fixed:esc} steps back. Length runs along the plane's X, width along its Y and height along its normal (a negative height grows the other way); the base is centred on the click unless you turn that off, then the click is a corner. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Cylinder
commands.summary: A cylinder standing on a plane at a position.
commands.details: Click a plane or a planar face for its centre, move the pointer to set the diameter and click (or type it, then {fixed:enter} or {fixed:tab}), then drag the arrow or type the height; {fixed:enter} adds it and {fixed:esc} steps back. Its axis is the plane's normal; a negative height grows the other way. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Sphere
commands.summary: A sphere centred on a plane at a position.
commands.details: Click a plane or a planar face for its centre, move the pointer to set the diameter and click; {fixed:enter} adds it and {fixed:esc} steps back. The plane runs through its middle. Combine it with other bodies to round off shapes. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Cone
commands.summary: A cone or a truncated cone standing on a plane at a position.
commands.details: Click a plane or a planar face for the centre of its base, move the pointer to set the base diameter and click (or type it, then {fixed:enter} or {fixed:tab}), then drag the arrow or type the height; {fixed:tab} from the height's box reaches the top diameter, which cuts the tip off above zero. {fixed:enter} adds it and {fixed:esc} steps back. Its axis is the plane's normal. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Torus
commands.summary: A ring centred on a plane at a position.
commands.details: Click a plane or a planar face for its centre, move the pointer to set the ring diameter (through the middle of the tube) and click (or type it, then {fixed:enter} or {fixed:tab}), then the tube's section diameter and click; {fixed:enter} adds it and {fixed:esc} steps back. The plane runs through the middle of the tube. Useful for O-rings and handles. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Extrude
commands.summary: Pulls sketch profiles or planar faces along their normal into a solid.
commands.details: Pick the profiles, then drag the arrow or type the distance; Symmetric splits it on both sides. All runs through every body in the way and ends at the last one, and To face stops at a face (extended past its edges), a plane or a vertex, with an end offset. The operation starts as Automatic: it cuts when the profile goes into material (the removed volume shows in red), joins when it touches a body and otherwise makes a new body, until you choose another. A curved or tilted start or end face can be followed or met flat at its nearest or farthest contact, and Sketch on face moves the profile onto the start face as a derived sketch.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Revolve
commands.summary: Turns sketch profiles about an axis into a solid.
commands.details: Pick the profiles, then click the axis in the view: a sketch line, an origin axis or a construction axis (an edge or a round face through the Axis box). The preview turns them a full 360 degrees at once; type another angle to change it, and Symmetric splits it on both sides. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Sweep
commands.summary: Moves a profile along a path into a solid.
commands.details: Pick one profile, then the path: sketch curves or edges. Keep the profile at the start of the path and smaller than its tightest bend. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Loft
commands.summary: Blends through two or more profiles, in the order they are picked.
commands.details: Pick the profiles one after another, usually on parallel planes. Straight sides makes ruled faces between them instead of a smooth skin. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Pipe
commands.summary: A round section along a path.
commands.details: Pick the path and set the diameter; Hollow adds a wall thickness. Good for cables, tubing and handrails. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Coil
commands.summary: A round or square section wound about an axis: springs and threads.
commands.details: Click a plane or a planar face for its axis, move the pointer to set the coil diameter (through the middle of the section) and click, then set the pitch between turns and the number of turns in the panel; {fixed:enter} adds it and {fixed:esc} steps back. Left-handed winds it the other way. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Thicken
commands.summary: Gives faces a thickness: a solid skin over the picked faces.
commands.details: Pick the faces, then drag the arrow or type the thickness; Other side grows it inward. Useful to turn a surface into a part. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Mesh to solid
commands.summary: Rebuilds a mesh body (STL, OBJ, 3MF or PLY) as a solid with smooth faces, and says how closely it follows the mesh.
commands.details: A mesh that is an extrusion or a revolution becomes a sketch of lines, arcs, circles and splines with an Extrude or Revolve feature, so a faceted cylinder becomes one circle extruded. Any other mesh becomes fitted planes, cylinders, cones, spheres and tori sewn into one solid. The panel previews the result with its match: the largest and mean deviation from the mesh, the share of the mesh within the tolerance, and the change in volume and area. Create solid adds it as one undo step, optionally removing the mesh.
commands.requires: Open or import a mesh first; a mesh opened for viewing is saved as an OPAD document first.

commands.title: Hole
commands.summary: Drills holes at sketch points, into the material behind the sketch.
commands.details: Pick the sketch points, then choose a simple, counterbored or countersunk hole with its diameter and depth. Each point gets one hole.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Fillet
commands.summary: Rounds edges.
commands.details: Pick the edges, then drag the arrow on the first edge or type the radius; edges that meet tangentially are rounded together. By rule… in the panel, or Select similar, picks every similar edge at once.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Chamfer
commands.summary: Bevels edges.
commands.details: Pick the edges, then drag the arrow on the first edge or type the distance, or two distances (Type) for an unequal bevel. Chamfers break sharp edges and ease assembly.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Shell
commands.summary: Hollows a body; the picked faces are removed and become openings.
commands.details: Pick the faces to open and set the wall thickness. To hollow it closed, click Bodies to hollow in the panel and pick the body.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Draft
commands.summary: Tilts faces about a neutral plane, for moulds.
commands.details: Pick the faces, the neutral plane and the angle. A few degrees of draft lets a part come out of its mould.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Press pull
commands.summary: Pushes planar faces in or pulls them out.
commands.details: Pick one or more faces and drag the arrow or type the distance; a negative value pushes into the material. The face moves straight along its normal: sides square to it extend, slanted sides do not (use Draft for those).
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Remove faces
commands.summary: Deletes faces and closes the gap by extending the faces around them.
commands.details: Pick the faces of a hole, fillet, chamfer or boss and press {fixed:enter}; the neighbouring faces grow until they meet. Imported bodies can be simplified this way. It is also on Press pull's menu and on the right-click menu of a picked face.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Scale
commands.summary: Resizes bodies uniformly.
commands.details: Set the factor: 2 doubles, 0.5 halves. Scale about the origin or about each body's centre of mass.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Combine
commands.summary: Joins, cuts or intersects bodies.
commands.details: Pick the target body (more through the Target bodies box), then the tool bodies, and choose the operation. Keep tools leaves the tool bodies in place after the cut.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Split body
commands.summary: Cuts bodies in two along a plane.
commands.details: Pick the bodies, then click the splitting plane in the view: an origin or a construction plane (a planar face through the Splitting plane box). Each body becomes two bodies in place, which you can then move, hide or delete.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Mirror
commands.summary: Makes mirrored copies of bodies about a plane.
commands.details: Pick the bodies and the mirror plane. Model half of a symmetric part and mirror the rest. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Rectangular pattern
commands.summary: Copies bodies in rows and columns.
commands.details: Pick the bodies, a direction, the count and the spacing; turn on a second direction for a grid. Changing the count later updates every copy. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Circular pattern
commands.summary: Copies bodies about an axis.
commands.details: Pick the bodies: the copies go round the Z axis at once; click another axis (an origin or construction axis, a sketch line) to turn them about it. Set the count and the total angle: 360 degrees spreads the copies evenly around a full turn. The Operation field makes a new body or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Point pattern
commands.summary: Copies bodies to a list of points.
commands.details: Pick the bodies, then the points: sketch points, vertices or points typed in. The bodies stand at the first point and a copy goes to every other one; set Bodies stand at to Origin when they were modelled at the origin, and every point gets a copy. Moving a point later moves its copy. The Operation field makes new bodies or joins, cuts or intersects existing ones, so one boss or hole can go to all the points at once.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Move / copy
commands.summary: Moves or copies bodies by distances and an optional turn.
commands.details: Pick the bodies, then drag an arrow of the triad on them (or its middle square, in the view's plane) or type X, Y and Z; with Grid snapping on, a drag goes in grid steps (hold {fixed:alt} to drag freely). Turn on Rotate for an axis and an angle: a ring round that axis through the bodies turns them in 5° steps, or type the angle. Make a copy leaves the original in place, and every value can be an expression. A part of a linked file moves the whole file as one, still linked.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Align
commands.summary: Puts a point, edge or face of bodies or components onto another point, edge, face or plane, moving and turning them as one.
commands.details: Pick the bodies or components, then what to align them by and where it goes: a face onto a face or a plane (the two come to face each other; Flip lays them flush), an edge or axis along another, or a point onto a point, a line or a plane. Motion keeps it to a move or to a turn only, Offset leaves a gap from the plane, and Turn about it spins them about the line or the plane's normal. Nothing is rebuilt: the objects move by their placement, keep their geometry, and stay aligned when the face or edge they were put on changes.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first; not available while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Remove
commands.summary: Takes bodies out of the design from this point on.
commands.details: The history keeps them: roll the timeline back before this step and they are there. Use it for tool bodies that are no longer needed.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Construction plane
commands.summary: A plane to sketch on, or to mirror, split and draft about.
commands.details: Make it offset from a plane (drag its arrow or type the distance), at an angle about an axis, midway between two planes, through three points or through a point normal to an axis. It follows its references when they change.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Construction axis
commands.summary: An axis to revolve or pattern about.
commands.details: Make it along an edge or through a round face's centre. Set Type to Two points to make it through two points, or to Normal for one normal to a plane through a point. Revolve and the circular pattern can pick it.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Interference check
commands.summary: Records an interference check in the history that runs again whenever its bodies change.
commands.details: It opens from Inspect > Interference: after a check, Keep as check fills it with that check's bodies and clearance. Pick the bodies, or none for all solids, and an optional clearance. With Fail on set, a finding marks the step as an error on the timeline.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Finish sketch
commands.summary: Ends the sketch and keeps it.
commands.details: The sketch becomes one step on the timeline and its closed regions turn into profiles for Extrude and Revolve. The camera and the ribbon return to where you were.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Cancel sketch
commands.summary: Leaves the sketch and discards the changes made since it opened.
commands.details: A new sketch is not created at all; an edited sketch goes back to how it was. If you changed the sketch, you confirm discarding first. Use Finish sketch to keep your work.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Sketch tools
commands.summary: Opens the sketch tool panel: the tool's steps and fields, precise input, constraints and snaps.
commands.details: Type exact coordinates there, absolute, relative or as length and angle, to place points. The other pages list the constraints and set the snaps and solver.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Command line
commands.summary: A line at the bottom left of the sketch for drafting by the keyboard: type a tool's name or a value.
commands.details: A word runs a tool or an editing command (its name or a short form such as LINE or REC); anything else goes into the step's value boxes, then {fixed:enter}. Up and Down recall earlier entries, and its close button hides it until this command ({key:sketch.commandLine}) opens it again.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Redefine sketch plane
commands.summary: Moves the sketch to another plane, keeping its geometry.
commands.details: Pick a new origin plane, planar face or construction plane, place the sketch origin on it and press OK. Features built on the sketch follow it to the new place.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Align sketch
commands.summary: Moves a sketch onto a face or plane, a point of it onto a point, or a line of it along a line.
commands.details: Select a sketch, or open it, and start: its own plane is what it aligns by, until you pick a point or a line of it instead. Pick where it goes and press {fixed:enter}: the sketch lies flush on the face or plane (Flip turns it over), Offset lifts it off, and Turn about it rotates it there. Put on a face it stays on that face as the face moves, and the features built on the sketch follow it.
commands.requires: Select a sketch first, or open one.

commands.title: Spline node weights
commands.summary: Edits the weights of a spline node and its handles.
commands.details: Select a node of a spline (or double-click it) and set the weights: the curve previews its new shape. Press {fixed:enter} or Apply to keep it. A heavier node pulls the curve closer to it.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Find open ends
commands.summary: Marks endpoints that meet nothing, which is why a profile is not closed.
commands.details: Each open end gets a red ring. Close the gaps by dragging the ends together or with Heal endpoints.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Construction
commands.summary: Turns the selected curves into construction geometry, or back.
commands.details: Construction curves are dashed: they guide and constrain but never form profiles. Use them for centre lines and helper circles.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Copy with base point
commands.summary: Copies the selected sketch curves about a point you click.
commands.details: Select the curves, run it and click the base point; a paste then carries the copy on the pointer by that point. The constraints among the curves come along.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open, with curves selected.

commands.title: Show or hide constraints
commands.summary: Shows or hides the constraint badges in the sketch.
commands.details: Hiding them only declutters the view: the constraints keep holding. Constraints in conflict and selected ones still show.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Select
commands.summary: Selects, drags and edits sketch geometry; double-click a dimension to change it.
commands.details: Dragging moves geometry while the constraints keep holding. {fixed:del} deletes the selection and Construction ({key:sketch.construction}) makes it construction geometry.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Line
commands.summary: Draws connected lines; click point after point.
commands.details: Each click ends one segment and starts the next. Close the loop on the start point, or press {fixed:enter} or double-click to stop; horizontal and vertical constraints are added as you draw.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Rectangle
commands.summary: Draws a rectangle from two opposite corners.
commands.details: Click the first corner, then the opposite one. Its sides get horizontal and vertical constraints, ready to dimension.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Centre rectangle
commands.summary: Draws a rectangle from its centre and a corner.
commands.details: Click the centre, then a corner; the rectangle grows symmetrically. Handy for parts centred on the origin.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: 3-point rectangle
commands.summary: Draws a rotated rectangle: a corner, the base direction, then the height.
commands.details: The first two clicks set one side at any angle. The third sets how far the opposite side lies.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Drafting workspace
commands.summary: Switches the ribbon to Drafting: 2D drawings (DXF, DWG, SVG) to draw on, measure, plot and turn into sketches.
commands.details: Viewing a drawing file comes here by itself, and the next other document goes back to where you were; arriving this way is not remembered for the next start. Draw on drawing started here opens a sketch on the drawing's own plane with its Sketch tab first in Drafting. The document and its timeline stay the same; only the ribbon's tabs change.

commands.title: Draw on drawing
commands.summary: Opens a sketch on the drawing's own plane and origin, to draw new curves over it with the sketch tools.
commands.details: Started in Drafting, its Sketch tab comes first there while it is open; started anywhere else, it opens in Design. Finish sketch keeps the curves as a sketch in the document; the drawing's own lines stay as they are. A file open in viewer mode is saved as an OPAD document, or copied, first. With drawings in several planes, select a layer of the one to draw on.
commands.requires: Open a 2D drawing (DXF, DWG or SVG) first; not while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Suppress
commands.summary: Suppresses the feature selected on the timeline, or brings back one that is suppressed.
commands.details: A suppressed feature stays in the history but adds nothing to the model, and the steps after it are computed without it; its marker is struck through. With no marker selected the feature that made the selected body is taken, else the command waits for a click on a marker.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Roll back to here
commands.summary: Shows the model as it was right after the step selected on the timeline.
commands.details: The playhead moves after that marker and a chip over the view says the model is rolled back; Roll forward to the end, or a click on the chip, shows every step again. A change made meanwhile is added at the end of the history. With no marker selected the command waits for a click on one.
commands.requires: Open an OPAD document; not while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Origin planes and axes
commands.summary: Shows the origin's XY, XZ and YZ planes and its axes in Design, also once there is a model.
commands.details: An empty document shows them anyway, with the grid, and there a plane picked in the view is where New sketch draws. With a model they are only shown, so clicks reach the faces; New sketch offers them to pick. The choice to show them is kept for the next start.
commands.requires: Open an OPAD document first.

commands.title: Named views
commands.summary: Lists the document's named views; choosing one returns to its camera.
commands.details: An exploded view kept with Save exploded view explodes again when chosen. Save view at the end of the list adds the current camera.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Rendering
commands.summary: How the view draws: small parts and quality while it moves, view animations and the theme.
commands.details: Its entries are Hide small parts while navigating, Small part size, Lower quality while navigating, Animate view changes and Dark theme. Preferences has the other display settings on its Display page.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Panels
commands.summary: Shows or hides the window's panels: the browser, annotations, the timeline, version control and the section.
commands.details: Each entry is the panel's own command with its key. Reset layout puts every panel back where it started.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Compare with a file
commands.summary: Compares another OPAD document, such as a copy or a variant, with this session.
commands.details: Choose the .opad file: Compare opens with it as A and this session as B, its changes listed in the panel and drawn in the view. The panel's pickers change either side afterwards.
commands.requires: Open an OPAD document; not while a sketch is open.

commands.title: Recover documents
commands.summary: Lists the snapshots an earlier session left behind, to restore, merge or compare them.
commands.details: Each snapshot is shown against its file as it is now, with Restore into file, Merge into current, Restore as copy, Compare, Discard snapshot and Later. With none left, the status bar says so.

commands.title: AI integration
commands.summary: Sets up local AI agent access to this window: the connection, what an agent may change and its activity.
commands.details: Enable local agent access, choose whether an agent may make design edits and exports, and copy the MCP server configuration for your AI client. The status bar's AI chip opens the same dialog.

commands.title: Agent activity
commands.summary: Shows what a connected AI agent is doing, with a button that stops its work.
commands.details: The panel lists the agent's requests as they come, and Follow changes shows its edits in the view. Stop agent work ends what it started.

commands.title: File types
commands.summary: Chooses which file types Windows opens with OPAD.
commands.details: Tick the formats and press Open with OPAD; they are registered for your Windows account only, and Default apps lets you make OPAD the app for a type. Elsewhere the system declares them, and the command opens the Files page of Preferences instead.

commands.title: Finish explode
commands.summary: Closes the Explode tab and its panel; the parts stay where they are.
commands.details: The exploded parts stay in place until Collapse exploded view brings them back. Exploded view opens the panel and the tab again.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Exploded view
commands.summary: Places a view of a saved exploded view on the sheet, with the parts where that view puts them.
commands.details: Save an exploded view first: Exploded view, then Save exploded view in its Explode tab; with several saved, a menu lists them. A frame follows the pointer and a click places it, seen from that view's camera. Thin phantom trail lines show where the parts came from and balloons point at the parts where they are drawn; when the exploded view is updated (Update view in the Explode panel), the drawing follows. A base view already placed switches between Assembled and a saved exploded view under View state in its context menu.
commands.requires: Only while a sheet is shown in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Publish PDF
commands.summary: Writes the sheets of a drawing as the pages of one PDF, from any workspace.
commands.details: With several drawings in the document a menu asks which one, then the file dialog asks where the PDF goes. Export sheet in Drawings > Output writes one sheet in the other formats.
commands.requires: Make a drawing first: New drawing in the Drawings workspace.

commands.title: Circle
commands.summary: Draws a circle from its centre and a point on it.
commands.details: Click the centre, then click again to set the size. Dimension the diameter afterwards to fix it.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: 2-point circle
commands.summary: Draws a circle across a diameter: two opposite points.
commands.details: Click one end of the diameter, then the other. Useful when the circle must touch two existing points.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: 3-point circle
commands.summary: Draws a circle through three points.
commands.details: Click three points on the circle, in any order. Snap to existing points to fit a circle through them.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Tangent circle
commands.summary: Draws a circle tangent to two lines with a set radius.
commands.details: Set the radius, pick the two lines, then click on the side where the circle should sit. It stays tangent when the lines move.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: 3-point arc
commands.summary: Draws an arc through a start, an end and a point on it.
commands.details: Click the start, the end, then move to bend the arc and click. The third click sets how far it bulges.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Centre arc
commands.summary: Draws an arc from its centre, a start and an end.
commands.details: Click the centre, then the start, which sets the radius, then sweep to the end and click. The arc runs the way the pointer went round, past half a turn too. A radius dimension fixes its size afterwards.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Tangent arc
commands.summary: Draws an arc that continues tangentially from the end of a line.
commands.details: Pick the line's endpoint, then click where the arc ends. The joint stays smooth when you edit either curve.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Ellipse
commands.summary: Draws an ellipse: centre, end of the first axis, then the second axis.
commands.details: The first axis can lie at any angle. The third click sets the half-width across it.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Slot
commands.summary: Draws a straight slot: two centres, then the width.
commands.details: Click the centre of each round end, then move sideways to set the width and click. The slot is one closed profile.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Centre slot
commands.summary: Draws a slot from its centre, the centre of one end and the width.
commands.details: Click the slot's centre, then the centre of one end; the other end mirrors it. The third click sets the width.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Arc slot
commands.summary: Draws a slot that follows an arc.
commands.details: Click the arc's centre, then the start and the end; the slot width comes from the panel. Useful for adjustment slots.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Polygon
commands.summary: Draws a regular polygon inscribed in a circle; set the number of sides in the panel.
commands.details: Click the centre, then a corner: the corners lie on the circle. The sides are kept equal by constraints.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Circumscribed polygon
commands.summary: Draws a regular polygon around a circle: the sides touch it.
commands.details: Click the centre, then the middle of a side. Use it when the size across flats matters, as for a hex nut.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Spline
commands.summary: Draws a smooth curve through the points you click; {fixed:enter} finishes.
commands.details: The curve updates as you add points. {fixed:alt}-click a finished spline to insert a node, and double-click a node to edit its weights.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Control-point spline
commands.summary: Draws a spline shaped by control points.
commands.details: The curve follows its thin grey control polygon without passing through its points. Set the degree in the panel; {fixed:enter} (Done) finishes.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Conic
commands.summary: Draws a conic between two ends, shaped by a tangent point and rho.
commands.details: Click the start and the point where the end tangents meet; the preview follows the pointer. Set rho (0 to 1, how sharp the curve is) before you click the end.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Point
commands.summary: Places points; holes are drilled at sketch points.
commands.details: Click to place a point, as many as you need. Points also serve as references for dimensions and constraints.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Text outlines
commands.summary: Writes text as sketch curves, ready to extrude or cut.
commands.details: Type the text, choose the font and height in the panel, then click the insertion point. Single-stroke fonts suit engraving.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: More create tools
commands.summary: Lists every Create tool in the Sketch menu, the ones under the ribbon's arrows too.
commands.details: Rotated rectangles, tangent arcs, slots, conics, text and more. Search commands ({key:tools.commands}) finds any of them by name too.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Trim
commands.summary: Removes the piece of a curve between intersections; it lights red before you click.
commands.details: Hover a curve to see which piece would go, then click. Keep clicking to clean up a whole outline.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Sketch fillet
commands.summary: Rounds the corner where two lines meet.
commands.details: Set the radius in the panel, then click near the corner. The arc is tangent to both lines and trims them.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Chamfer
commands.summary: Bevels a corner by two distances.
commands.details: Pick the corner and set the two distances: the bevel previews; press {fixed:enter} or Apply. Equal distances on a square corner give a 45 degree bevel.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Offset
commands.summary: Copies a connected chain of curves at a distance; drag the arrow or type it.
commands.details: Click one curve and the whole connected chain is taken. Drag the arrow, or type the distance, then apply; negative goes to the other side.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Mirror
commands.summary: Mirrors curves about a line.
commands.details: Select the curves to mirror (click or drag a window), press {fixed:enter}, click the mirror line and press {fixed:enter} again. The copies get symmetric constraints, so they follow the originals.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Move
commands.summary: Moves the selected curves by an offset.
commands.details: Select the curves, set the X and Y offset and apply. A preview shows the result first.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Rotate
commands.summary: Rotates the selected curves about a point.
commands.details: Select the curves, set the centre and the angle and apply. A preview shows the result first.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Scale
commands.summary: Resizes the selected curves about a point.
commands.details: Select the curves, set the centre and the factor and apply. A factor of 2 doubles every length.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Copy with offset
commands.summary: Copies the selected curves at an offset.
commands.details: Select the curves, set the X and Y offset and apply. The originals stay where they are.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Rectangular pattern
commands.summary: Copies the selected curves in rows and columns, kept as an editable pattern.
commands.details: Select the curves, set the counts and spacings, preview and apply. Select a copy later and open the tool again to change the pattern.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Polar pattern
commands.summary: Copies the selected curves around a centre, kept as an editable pattern.
commands.details: Select the curves, set the centre, the count and the angle, preview and apply. Bolt circles are a typical use.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Split curve
commands.summary: Splits a curve in two at the point you click.
commands.details: Click inside the curve where it should split. Both pieces stay joined at the new point.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Extend curve
commands.summary: Extends a curve to the next boundary curve.
commands.details: Pick the curve near the end to extend, then the boundary curve. The end moves until it meets the boundary.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Break at intersections
commands.summary: Breaks the selected curves at every intersection.
commands.details: Each piece between crossings becomes its own curve. Useful before trimming or before deleting parts of imported drawings.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Region union
commands.summary: Joins two closed loops into one outline.
commands.details: Click inside the first loop, then inside the second, and apply. The result replaces both loops with one clean outline.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Region subtract
commands.summary: Cuts the second closed loop out of the first.
commands.details: Click inside the first loop, then inside the second, and apply. The result replaces both loops with one clean outline.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Region intersection
commands.summary: Keeps only the area two closed loops share.
commands.details: Click inside the first loop, then inside the second, and apply. The result replaces both loops with one clean outline.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Heal endpoints
commands.summary: Merges endpoints closer than the gap tolerance.
commands.details: Set the gap tolerance and apply: nearby ends are joined so profiles close. Imported drawings often need it.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Explode pattern
commands.summary: Turns the copies of a pattern into independent curves.
commands.details: Select a patterned curve and apply. The pattern can no longer be edited as one, but each copy can be changed on its own.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Dimension
commands.summary: Adds a driving dimension: pick geometry, place the value, type it.
commands.details: Pick a line, a circle, an arc or two points, click where the label goes, then type a value or an expression. The geometry resizes to match; a dimension the solver cannot satisfy is refused.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Horizontal
commands.summary: Makes a line horizontal, or two points level.
commands.details: Pick a line, or two points. A level-bar badge shows the constraint; select it and press {fixed:del} to remove it.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Vertical
commands.summary: Makes a line vertical, or two points one above the other.
commands.details: Pick a line, or two points. An upright-bar badge shows the constraint; select it and press {fixed:del} to remove it.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Coincident
commands.summary: Joins a point to another point or onto a curve.
commands.details: Pick the point, then the point or curve it should lie on. Endpoints that share a point form a connected profile.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Collinear
commands.summary: Puts two lines on one straight line.
commands.details: Pick both lines. They may still have a gap between them.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Parallel
commands.summary: Makes one line parallel to another.
commands.details: Pick the two lines; they turn parallel, each moving as little as it can, and a line held by other constraints stays put. Dimension the distance between them to fix it.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Perpendicular
commands.summary: Makes two lines meet at a right angle.
commands.details: Pick the two lines; they need not touch. A ⊥ badge shows the constraint.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Tangent
commands.summary: Makes a line and an arc, or two arcs, meet smoothly.
commands.details: Pick the two curves; they touch without a kink. Use it where a slot or a fillet meets straight sides.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Equal
commands.summary: Makes two lines equally long, or two arcs or circles the same size.
commands.details: Pick both curves. One dimension then drives both.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Smooth spline join (G2)
commands.summary: Joins a spline to a line, an arc or another spline with matching curvature (G2).
commands.details: Pick the line, circle, arc or spline, then the control-point spline that joins it, near their shared end. Stronger than Tangent: the curvature also flows on, which reflects light without a visible seam. Both curves move as little as they can; one held by other constraints, such as Fix, stays put.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Equal endpoint curvature
commands.summary: Gives a spline's end the curvature of the line, arc or spline it meets.
commands.details: Pick the line, circle, arc or spline, then the control-point spline. By a line the spline's end runs straight; by an arc it bends as the arc does. A curve held by other constraints, such as Fix, stays put. Use it with Tangent for smooth spline transitions.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Concentric
commands.summary: Gives two circles or arcs the same centre.
commands.details: Pick the two circles or arcs. Use it for bosses around holes and for washers.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Midpoint
commands.summary: Puts a point in the middle of a line.
commands.details: Pick the point, then the line. The point stays centred when the line changes length.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Symmetric
commands.summary: Makes two points symmetric about a line.
commands.details: Pick the two points, then the line of symmetry. Use a construction centre line for symmetric parts.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Fix
commands.summary: Locks points or curves where they are.
commands.details: Fixed geometry no longer moves when you drag or dimension other curves. Select its badge and press {fixed:del} to free it.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Constraints
commands.summary: Lists the sketch's constraints and dimensions; select one to highlight it.
commands.details: Filter the list by type, switch a dimension between driving and reference, or delete it. The status bar shows how many degrees of freedom remain.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: More constraints
commands.summary: Lists every constraint tool in the Sketch menu, the ones under the ribbon's arrows too.
commands.details: Equal, concentric, midpoint, symmetric, collinear and the spline continuity constraints are here. Search commands ({key:tools.commands}) finds any of them by name too.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: More modify tools
commands.summary: Lists every Modify tool in the Sketch menu, the ones under the ribbon's arrows too.
commands.details: Move, rotate, scale, patterns, split, extend, region booleans and healing are here. Search commands ({key:tools.commands}) finds any of them by name too.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Project
commands.summary: Projects body edges, faces or vertices onto the sketch as reference curves.
commands.details: Pick edges, or faces, vertices and bodies with the panel's Pick filter, then press {fixed:enter} or Apply: they are flattened onto the sketch plane. Linked projections follow the body when it changes; an editable copy does not.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Body-plane intersection
commands.summary: Adds the curves where bodies cut the sketch plane.
commands.details: Pick the bodies, or choose them in the panel, then press {fixed:enter} or Apply. Useful to sketch on the section of an existing part.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Silhouette
commands.summary: Adds the outline of bodies as seen along the sketch normal.
commands.details: Pick the bodies, then press {fixed:enter} or Apply. Handy for covers, gaskets and cut-outs that follow a part's shape.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Include reference curves
commands.summary: Brings other sketches' curves and construction axes into this sketch as references.
commands.details: Choose the source in the panel or pick it in the view, then press {fixed:enter} or Apply: its curves come in as construction geometry flattened onto the sketch plane. Linked references follow their source when it changes.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Break projection link
commands.summary: Makes a linked projection editable.
commands.details: Select the projected curves and press {fixed:enter} or Apply: they stop following the body and become normal sketch curves. The link cannot be restored afterwards.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: More reference tools
commands.summary: Lists every reference tool: projections, intersections, silhouettes and included curves.
commands.details: Reference curves come from bodies and other sketches. Search commands ({key:tools.commands}) finds any of them by name too.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Insert image
commands.summary: Places an image on the sketch plane as a backdrop to trace over.
commands.details: Choose the file and set the width, click the insertion point (the image's lower-left corner), then press {fixed:enter} or Apply. Calibrate image then scales it to a known distance.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Transform image
commands.summary: Moves, scales, rotates or fades a backdrop image.
commands.details: Drag the image in the view to move it, or choose it and type its position, width, rotation and opacity, then press {fixed:enter} or Apply. The image is a view aid and is never part of a profile.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Calibrate image
commands.summary: Scales a backdrop image by a distance you know.
commands.details: Click two points on the image, type their real distance over the measured one, then press {fixed:enter} or Apply. Trace and dimension after calibrating so the sizes are right.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Trace image
commands.summary: Turns the dark or light areas of a backdrop image into editable curves.
commands.details: Set the threshold, smoothing and tolerance, preview and apply. Clean, high-contrast images trace best.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Remove image
commands.summary: Removes a backdrop image from the sketch.
commands.details: Curves traced from it stay. Undo brings the image back.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Simplify curves
commands.summary: Replaces dense polylines with fewer lines and arcs within a tolerance.
commands.details: Set the curve tolerance, preview and apply. Traced images and imported meshes become much lighter to edit.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Import SVG / DXF
commands.summary: Imports the curves of an SVG or DXF file into the sketch.
commands.details: Choose the file and the curve tolerance and apply. The curves become normal sketch geometry you can constrain.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Export SVG / DXF
commands.summary: Writes the sketch's curves to an SVG or DXF file.
commands.details: Choose the file name and apply. Use it for laser cutting, plotters and other CAD tools.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Images and files
commands.summary: Lists the image and file tools: backdrop images, tracing, simplify and SVG or DXF import and export.
commands.details: Start with Insert image to trace a photo or a scan. Search commands ({key:tools.commands}) finds any of them by name too.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Snaps
commands.summary: Chooses which points, alignments and angles the cursor is pulled to.
commands.details: Endpoints, midpoints, centres, quadrants, intersections, the grid and angle steps can each be turned off. The solver's tolerance and iterations are set here too.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Selection
commands.summary: Selection options: filter by type, select a connected chain or all of a type.
commands.details: Set the filter to Arcs, for example, and a window selects only arcs. The page also holds construction, open ends and node tools.
commands.requires: Only while a sketch is open: start one with New sketch.

commands.title: Simulate workspace
commands.summary: Switches to the Simulate workspace: joints, mechanisms, motion and dynamic studies, loads and structural studies.
commands.details: Its Mechanism tab joins parts with joints and runs motion and dynamic studies (Project Chrono); its Structure tab puts loads and supports on faces and runs static stress and vibration studies (Netgen and CalculiX). The browser's Simulation folder lists the joints, the load cases and the studies, and the Simulation panel moves the mechanism and plays the results.

commands.title: Gear
commands.summary: Makes an involute gear: a spur gear, an internal ring gear or a rack, with standard teeth of the module you give.
commands.details: The pitch diameter is the module times the teeth, and two gears mesh with their centres the sum of their pitch radii apart (an internal pair: the difference). Phase turns the teeth so a second gear meets the first's gaps, and Bore or Rim add the hole or the outer ring. Gear relations in the Simulate workspace then turn the gears together.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Simulation panel
commands.summary: Opens the Simulation panel: the mechanism's joints on a slider, new joints and relations, and the studies with their results.
commands.details: Drag the slider to move the mechanism through the chosen joint; it is written to the document when you let go. Choose a study and press Run, then play its frames, step through them or click the chart. A structural study's result map colours the parts by stress, displacement or mode shape.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Joint
commands.summary: Joins the picked part to the part it moves in, or to the world, with the joint kind chosen in the Simulation panel.
commands.details: Pick a circular edge, a cylindrical or flat face or a vertex of the moving part first: it sets the joint's axis and origin, and a second pick on another part makes that part the base. Revolute turns about the axis, slider moves along it, and ball, planar, cylindrical, screw, rigid and ground joints are there too. Gear, rack and pinion and lead screw relations couple two joints picked in the Simulation folder.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Motion study
commands.summary: Makes and runs a kinematic study that drives the chosen joint a full turn (or 50 mm) in two seconds.
commands.details: The parts follow through the joints and relations at every frame, with each joint's value, speed and acceleration recorded. Play the frames in the view or plot any series in the Simulation panel. The study keeps its settings, so an agent or Run again repeats it on the changed model.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Dynamic study
commands.summary: Makes and runs a dynamic study with Project Chrono: one second under gravity with the joints' drives, springs and friction.
commands.details: Masses and inertias come from the bodies' volumes and materials, and joints with a drive turn as their motors make them. Reactions, motor torques and power, energies and the joints' values are recorded for the chart. Contacts between parts and other settings are set through the study's settings.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Static stress study
commands.summary: Makes and runs a static stress study of the first load case with Netgen and CalculiX.
commands.details: The bodies are meshed with quadratic tetrahedra, the case's supports, forces, pressures and bolt preloads are applied, and CalculiX solves for displacements and stresses. The result map shows von Mises stress or displacement over the deformed parts, and the summary gives each body's safety factor against its material's yield strength.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Vibration modes study
commands.summary: Makes and runs a study of the natural frequencies and mode shapes of the first load case's supported bodies.
commands.details: Only the case's supports count: the bodies vibrate freely about them. Each mode is listed with its frequency, and the result map shows its shape on the parts. Resonance is likely where a running speed or a forcing frequency is near one of them.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Heat source
commands.summary: Adds the heat a part gives off, in W, to the thermal load case.
commands.details: Pick the part (it warms through its whole volume, like a chip or a coil) or the faces the heat comes through, then type the power. A thermal study needs at least one heat source or fixed temperature.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Fixed temperature
commands.summary: Holds the picked faces at a temperature, in °C.
commands.details: For a face on a cold plate, in water or against a part kept at a known temperature. The heat that flows into it is reported.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Convection
commands.summary: Lets the air carry heat away from the picked parts or faces.
