commands.details: Natural: still air, its film coefficient found for each face from its size, its tilt and the gap to the face it looks at (fins), solved with the temperatures. Forced: air moving along the faces at a speed you give. Or a film coefficient you know, in W/m²K.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Radiation
commands.summary: Lets the picked parts or faces radiate heat to their surroundings.
commands.details: Type the surface's emissivity: bare aluminium about 0.1, anodised or painted about 0.85. It matters most for hot parts in still air.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Fan
commands.summary: Puts a fan on a heatsink: its air flows along the fins and carries their heat away.
commands.details: Pick the heatsink, choose a fan (typical fans by size and speed, or type its free flow and shut-off pressure) and the way the air goes along the fins. The study finds the fins in the heatsink's shape, where the fan's curve meets the fins' pressure drop, the heat transfer in the channels and how much the air warms. Inside a vented box, with the air solved, pick instead a block that stands for the fan: the fan blows from its middle.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Thermal setup
commands.summary: Sets up a thermal study of a board, its chips and a heatsink in a vented box step by step: the box, the heat, the fans or the vents, and the run with the air solved.
commands.details: Its first page picks the bodies the box is made of, one or several (a base and its lid, a frame and its panels), found around the parts that make heat; click bodies in the view or rows in the browser to add or take them out, and on an empty document it builds an example. Tick the parts that make heat with their power (a chip joined into its board: pick its face in the view), the board (its copper layers spread the heat), and the fans or vents only (warm air rising): each fan picked as a body or a component (its own model as one part), the flat face its air goes through, its model or its datasheet's flow and pressure, and the heatsink it blows through (a body or a component) with one material. Run solves the air in the box and around it with OpenFOAM and the parts with CalculiX: each part's temperature, the fans' flow and the air through the box, with streamlines.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Thermal study
commands.summary: Makes and runs a thermal study: the temperatures of the parts from their heat sources and cooling.
commands.details: Steady finds where the temperatures settle; Over time shows how fast the parts warm up, from the room's temperature. The panel gives each part's hottest temperature, where the heat goes and each fan's flow, pressure and air temperature rise; the result map colours the parts by temperature.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Simulation guide
commands.summary: Opens step-by-step use cases of the Simulate tools, each with buttons that start the tools it uses.
commands.details: Ten use cases: a hinged part moved with the slider, a mechanism's travel in a motion study, gears and lead screws, a part swinging or falling under gravity, whether a part holds under a load, a bolted joint, natural frequencies, a 3D-printed part, a part kept cool and a board in a vented box. Each says what you get, the steps with your keys, and a tip. The Simulation panel's Step-by-step guides button opens the one for where your document is.

commands.title: Printed part
commands.summary: Sets a structural study's bodies as 3D printed: filament, layers, walls, skins and infill, typed in or read from a slicer's profile.
commands.details: Each printed body is split into its walls, its top and bottom skins and its infill, and each gets the stiffness and strength of printed roads: along a road, across it and between layers. Import slicer profile reads PrusaSlicer .ini, OrcaSlicer and Bambu Studio .json, Cura .cfg, a .3mf project or the settings a slicer appended to its G-code. The summary gives the printed mass and how and on which layer the part fails first; the result map adds the failure index (Tsai-Hill in the layer, a quadratic criterion between layers: 1 fails). The filament values are typical printed-specimen data: adjust them from your own test bars through the study's settings.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Run study
commands.summary: Runs the chosen study on the model as it is now and shows its results.
commands.details: Motion and dynamic studies play their frames when they finish, and a static or modal study shows its result map. The study's summary is kept in the document so the timeline, the diff and an agent can read it. A run of an unchanged model and study is answered from memory at once.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Play
commands.summary: Plays the frames of the motion or dynamic study shown, or pauses them.
commands.details: A study of a second or more plays in real time, and a shorter one is stretched to three seconds. The parts are only shown moved: the document keeps them where they are. Drag the frame slider or click the chart to stop at a moment.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Fixed support
commands.summary: Holds the picked faces still in the load case: a wall the parts are fixed to.
commands.details: Static and modal studies need the parts held, by a fixed support or by balanced loads. Pick the faces first, then the command adds the support to the last load case. It is listed in the browser's Simulation folder under its case.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Force
commands.summary: Puts a force on the picked faces, spread over them, in the load case.
commands.details: Type the force as x, y and z in newtons: it is shared over the faces by their areas. Pick the faces first, then the command asks for the vector. Static studies of the case take it.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Pressure
commands.summary: Puts a pressure on the picked faces in the load case.
commands.details: Type the pressure in MPa: a positive one pushes into the faces, a negative one pulls them out. It acts square to each face, curved ones too. Static studies of the case take it.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Bolt preload
commands.summary: Pretensions the picked bolt in the load case: its shank is cut and pulled together with the force you give.
commands.details: Pick the bolt's body: its largest cylinder is taken as the shank. The static study reports the shank's axial stress against preload over area, and the clamped parts feel the bolt's grip. Add the service loads to the same case to see what they add.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Gravity load
commands.summary: Adds the parts' own weight to the load case, at standard gravity down the Z axis.
commands.details: Every element is loaded by its mass from the body's material. Pick nothing for it: it acts on all the bodies of the study. Combine it with supports and other loads in the same case.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.

commands.title: Result map
commands.summary: Shows the structural study's result as colours over the deformed parts, with a legend, or hides it.
commands.details: Choose the field in the Simulation panel: von Mises stress or displacement for a static study, a mode for a modal one. The deformation is scaled up so it can be seen, and the legend says by how much. The bodies under the map are hidden while it shows.
commands.requires: Open or create a document first.
